The dedication of the church of Saint Peter is perhaps suggested by the words of the second prayer: “to whom [Peter] this basilica is consecrated.” It should further be noted that the compiler arbitrarily included this Mass among the common Masses in April; hence it cannot be concluded from this passage with certainty that the dedication of the Basilica of Saint Peter, or another feast of that apostle, fell in April.]

AT THE DEDICATION.

XXXIV. Another.

God, who everywhere make the dignity of the blessed apostle Peter glorious, grant, we ask, that we may always be cherished both by his teaching and by his merits. Through [him], etc.

Receive, Lord, we ask, the offerings that we bring to your majesty in honor of the blessed apostle Peter, to whom this basilica is consecrated, and protect us through his prayers. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. You grant that the power of the blessed apostle Peter be magnified in every place of your dominion, not only where his venerable relics rest, but wherever he is invoked with precious reverence; now also show to endure that his sound goes out into all the earth and saving words run throughout the whole world. Through [him], etc.

We bless your mercies, Lord, who continually permit us to be cherished by the remembrance of your blessed apostle Peter, as we humbly beseech you that we may experience the patronage of him whose solemnity we celebrate. Through [him], etc.

16 XXXV. Another.

“If you will, you can make me clean,” Lord; and grant us through the prayers of your saints the forgiveness which the voice of our iniquity does not obtain. Through [him], etc.

We humbly ask you, Lord, that although our offenses hinder us, our offering may nevertheless not be displeasing because of the remembrance of your martyrs. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. With humbled heart we ask that, although our crimes are so great that we struggle even with the innumerable intercessions of the saints, you may nevertheless, in your boundless mercy, grant that our sins not prevail more than the abundant satisfaction of the righteous on our behalf. Through [him], etc.

Grant, Lord, we ask, that although we are weighed down by immense errors and have no confidence in conscience, the blessed supplication of your martyrs may come to our aid. Through [him], etc.

[Col. 0034A] XXXVI. Another.

May the multiplied patronage of the saints profit us, Lord, and may the many prayers of the blessed poured out for us dissolve our injustices.

[Note: [Col. 0034D] “For those without merit” would be preferable.]

Do not despise, Lord, we ask, the gifts brought for our transgressions; rather, through the intercession of your saints, turn toward forgiveness those who beseech you. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. For you distinguish your people, Lord; and when a multitude gathers for the festivals of the martyrs, you know those who belong truly to the number of your faithful. Therefore let no one remain in the portion of the devil who desires to be numbered among the lot of the saints. Through [him], etc.

[Note: [Col. 0034D] The words “a multitude gathers for the festivals of the martyrs” are sewn in here; or something should be supplied before “for the martyrs,” for example “when.”]

Grant, we ask, Lord, that your holy martyrs lend us the help of their intercession, so that we may escape your anger, which we have deserved by our wickedness. Through [him], etc.

XXXVII. Another.

We ask, Lord, that we not be overwhelmed, although by immense masses of sins; everywhere we entreat you, while your saints intercede, that, though offended by our evils, you not reject the offerings now present, but perfect us as pleasing to you through the power of the sacrament. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. We humbly beseech you to grant that, just as your saints conquered the world through your power, so they may ask that we be freed from worldly errors. Through [him], etc.

Since our voices, Lord, do not deserve to be heard, we ask that the intercession of your saints be accepted—or, according to the variant inserted into the text, “become pleasing”—on our behalf. Through [him], etc.

XXXVIII. Another.

Receive our prayers with favor, Lord, and guard us through the intercession of your saints, so that we may serve worthily at your altars. Through [him], etc.

Grant us, Lord, we ask, to serve your gifts with a free mind, so that, as your grace purifies us, we may be restored by the same mysteries through which we serve. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. For a sacred festival is celebrated for you, Lord; a day consecrated to you is observed, which the blood of your blessed martyrs, poured out in testimony to your truth, marked with the glorious honor of your name. Through [him], etc.

Almighty and everlasting God, who, caring for our frailty, console us through the continual celebration of the saints, grant us, established under such patrons, both to be fortified with perpetual security and to rejoice in saving progress. Through [him], etc.

[Note: [Col. 0034D] This is another Mass, although it is not distinguished by a separate number.]

May our gifts be pleasing to you, Lord, gifts both established by your commands and commended by the glorious festival of your saints. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. For we admire your powers and your victories, Lord, whenever in your Church we celebrate the solemnities of these days, which the palms of your distinguished confessors and martyrs have consecrated for perpetual remembrance and holy joy among the faithful peoples. Through [him], etc.

We ask, Lord our God, that we may follow in deed and understanding the divine mysteries that we frequently celebrate in memory of your saints. Through [him], etc.

18 Be present, Lord, with your patronage to your people as they beseech you, so that what they do not presume upon through confidence in themselves they may obtain through the merits of those who intercede. Through [him], etc.

XXXIX. Another.

Almighty and everlasting God, who perceive that we are not fit to beseech your majesty as we ought, grant that your holy martyrs may intercede for our sins—those whom you can worthily hear. Through [him], etc.

Help us, Lord, through the prayer of your saints, so that we may experience the help of those whose festivals we celebrate. Through [him], etc.

May the appointed protections of the holy martyrs commend the offering of your household, and, so that it may be pleasing to you, may it be offered through supplications that please you. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. You not only paid the debt of the ancient death, to which you yourself were not subject, repaying it on behalf of those who owed it, but also granted your martyrs that what human nature had contracted by acting against the will of its Creator, and had been destined to discharge under the law imposed upon it, should become righteousness for them when they willingly accepted it for the testimony of their Creator, and that punishment should pass over into glory. Through [him], etc.

[Note: [Col. 0035D] This same preface is repeated in the first Mass of Saints John and Paul; there, instead of “they accepted,” one reads “they accept,” where perhaps “martyrdom” is understood.]

XL. Another.

May the votive sacrifices of your people be pleasing to you, Lord, and may the supplication of those for whose glory they are brought obtain what our frailty cannot obtain.

[Note: [Col. 0035D] In the second Mass of the same martyrs, John and Paul, where this prayer is likewise read, “of the saints” occurs instead of “of those.”]

May the satisfaction of your saints follow the gifts dedicated to your name, Lord, on our behalf, so that through those who are worthy in your sight our offenses may be forgiven.

[Note: [Col. 0035D] In the same second Mass: “that they may be pleasing to you” occurs instead.]

It is truly right. To achieve a greater triumph over the enemy of the human race, you brought it about that, besides that singular glory by which he was overthrown in ineffable ways through the power of the Lord, he should also be overcome by the holy martyrs; and that in his members as well there should follow the victory that preceded in the head. Through [him], etc.

[Note: [Col. 0035D] Elsewhere, in the same second Mass: “by the power of the Lord himself.”]

[Note: [Col. 0035D] In the same Mass there is a better reading, fitting our Leo: “and the same victory should follow in the members that preceded in the head.” Besides this reading, a variant reading of this passage is also given there.]

XLI. Another.

Hear our prayers, Lord; and grant us the help of your saints, so that the gifts we offer may be worthy in the sight of your majesty. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. For it is your work and your power, Lord, that the enemy of human nature should be made subject not only through your Son, our Lord, but also through your holy martyrs, to the nature whose debtor he once was, and that he who had been subjected to it should himself be subjected. And therefore, with the angels, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0036D] This preface is repeated in the third Mass of Saints John and Paul, with the word “its” omitted.]

XLII. Another.

We ask, Lord our God, that our sins not weigh us down before your justice, which your unconquerable mercy …; and do not permit us, however burdened by countless errors, to be crushed, since you have willed that we be aided by such great intercessions of your saints. Through [him], etc.

[Note: [Col. 0036D] The Roman Missal gives this prayer on 23 July, the feast of Saint Apollinaris.]

Look favorably, Lord, upon these gifts, which we bring both for the commemoration of your saints and as an offering for our offenses. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. For in your blessed martyrs, the glorious confession of your faith fought against the world’s profanation; wise and holy endurance against the irrational savagery of the persecutors; the hope—or, according to the variant reading, “the promise”—of heavenly rewards against temporal allurements; the eternity of coming salvation against attachment to the present life; and in all things they conquered the roaring schemes of the devil, while your right hand fought in them. Through [him], etc.

XLIII. Another.

Make our offerings pleasing to you, Lord, by your gracious favor; for there is nothing in us that can appease you unless, while the saints intercede, your propitiation goes before us. Through [him], etc.

[Col. 0036C] It is truly right. Recalling the praises of the venerable martyrs: for it is your work and your power, Lord, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0036D] As in the preface of the first Mass of the seventh series, where only the words “our Lord” are omitted.]

Strengthened, Lord, both by the birthdays of the saints and by the gift of the sacrament, we ask that we may enjoy eternally the good things by which we are now cherished through your grace. Through [him], etc.

May your propitiation be present, Lord, we ask, to your suppliant people, so that what they faithfully seek under your inspiration they may receive through your swift generosity. Through [him], etc.

IN THE MONTH OF MAY. IX. PRAYERS FOR THE ASCENSION OF THE LORD.

[Note: [Col. 0036D] This prayer occurs in Book I, no. 64, of the Gelasian Sacramentary, and also in the Gregorian, on the Ascension of the Lord.]

Be present to our supplications, Lord, so that, just as we trust that the Savior of the human race has sat with you in your majesty, so we may perceive him remaining with us until the end of the age, as you promised. Through [him], etc.

[Col. 0037A] Almighty and everlasting God, grant us, through the gift of today’s festival, that the intention of your children may be directed there where our substance is with you in your Only-Begotten Son. Through [him], etc.

Hear us, merciful God, and grant that our minds may be raised to where our Redeemer ascended, so that at the second coming of the Mediator we may receive as a manifest gift what we now dare to hope has been promised. Through [him], etc.

[Note: [Col. 0037D] In the same Gregorian Sacramentary on the same day, and also in the Roman Missal.]

Grant us, almighty and merciful God, that what we have received while celebrating in visible mysteries we may attain in invisible effect. Through [him], etc.

Grant us, Lord, not to set our minds on earthly things, but to love heavenly things, and, though placed amid passing things, to cling even now to those that endure. Through [him], etc.

[Col. 0037B] Hear us, God our Savior, because through these sacred mysteries—or, according to the variant reading, “through these exchanges”—we trust that what preceded in the Head has to be accomplished in the whole body of the Church, through the same Jesus Christ our Lord.

I.

[Note: [Col. 0037D] It occurs in the Ambrosian Missal in Pamelius, volume I, p. 374. This first preface appears to be Leonine, as does the third.]

It is truly right. After his resurrection, glorious for all ages, he appeared visibly to his disciples and tangible to their touch until the fortieth day; and before their eyes he was lifted up into heaven. During this interval the beginnings of the Church advanced, so that what they had believed might become more certain and what they were to teach might be learned more fully. Through [him], etc.

II.

It is truly right. We ought to rejoice with fitting exultation amid the joys of today’s festival, because the Ascension into heaven of the Mediator between God and humanity, the man Jesus Christ, was not a departure from our lowliness: he remains both in that glory which he always had with you and in that nature which he made his own from us. Thus he deigned to become human so that he might grant us to be participants in his divinity. Therefore, etc.

III.

It is truly right. For, while the angels and the princes of the angels looked on in wonder, the King of glory and Lord of powers placed at your right hand the firstfruits of the blessed resurrection, offered to the throne of your majesty. And therefore, etc.

21 Sharing in communion and celebrating the most sacred day of the Ascension into heaven of our Lord Jesus Christ, and also venerating the memory, etc.

IV. Another.

It is truly right. And we humbly beseech you to grant by your inspiration that our minds may be raised to where our Redeemer ascended, so that at the second coming of the Mediator we may receive as a manifest gift what we now dare to hope has been promised, through this same Jesus Christ our Lord, through whom the angels praise you, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0037D] It occurs in Book I, no. 63, of the Gelasian Sacramentary.]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the intention of our mind may always be directed to where the glorious author of today’s solemnity entered, and that we may reach by our manner of life the place toward which we proceed by faith. Through [him], etc.

V. Another.

Look upon the exaltation of our condition—or, according to the variant reading, “of human substance”—God, so that, cleansed by your gracious favor, we may be prepared for the sacraments of your great compassion. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. Kindly pour this into our understanding: lest, clinging to earthly affections, we fail to raise our eyes to heavenly things; lest, occupied with low desires, we be unable to lift our minds to where our Savior ascended; lest, following the devil’s footsteps, we withdraw from fellowship with Christ. For no one can delight in the loftiness of the highest and true King unless, having destroyed—or, according to the variant reading, “overthrown”—the pestilential rights of the Tyrant, he tramples them underfoot. Through [him], etc.

VI. Another.

[Note: [Col. 0037D] It occurs in Menard’s edition of the Gregorian Sacramentary on the Ascension of the Lord. A similar thought occurs in Leo, *Sermon 1 on the Ascension of the Lord*, chapter 4: “Since therefore Christ’s ascension is our advancement, and where the glory of the Head has gone before, there the hope of the body is called.”]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the members of your faithful may follow to where our Head and origin has gone before. Through [him], etc.

It is truly right. On this day Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, having brought the divine mystery to its appointed completion, unfolded the gift of the ancient dispensation: namely, that through the human being whom he had subjugated he might overthrow the devil, the enemy of the heavenly work, and restore human substance to heavenly gifts. Through [him], etc.

[Note: [Col. 0038D] In Book I, no. 64, of the Gelasian Sacramentary, and in Pamelius, volume II, p. 569, where this preface is read, “he fulfilled” is perhaps better than “he explained.”]

[Note: [Col. 0038D] Gregorian manuscripts give this prayer on Wednesday in the week of white garments.]

Grant, we ask, Lord, that the affection of our Christian devotion may tend there where our substance is with you. Through [him], etc.

[Col. 0038C] Sharing in communion and celebrating the most sacred day on which our Lord, your Only-Begotten Son, placed at the right hand of your glory the human being of our substance united to himself; and also venerating the memory, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0038D] In the Gelasian Sacramentary, Book I, no. 63, it stands in the same words. In the Gregorian and Roman Missal, the only change is: “the substance of our frailty united to himself.”]

X. PRAYERS FOR THE EVE OF PENTECOST.

God, who, if you were to repay what we deserve, would find us failing before we endured the punishments we merit, we ask you, appeased, to absolve our errors and, so that we may be able to turn to your commandments, to go before us with abundant propitiation. Through [him], etc.

Clement, almighty, and merciful God, turn away the hardness of our heart, by which we fear the repeated blows but do not perceive the gifts bestowed through such great mysteries; and grant us by your inspiration both to ask forgiveness for our sins and to render thanks for our salvation. Through [him], etc.

Lord our God, whose first cause is mercy, that we may fear and love your name, mercifully pour this into our hearts: rejecting what does not please you, may we submit to you with sincere will. Through [him], etc.

Spare, Lord, spare those who sin; and so that we may be able to approach your propitiation, grant us the Spirit who corrects. Through [him], etc.

[Note: [Col. 0039C] This formula, “Another,” omitted by Muratorius, occurs in the codex. It is indeed a distinct Mass, instituted after the fast had been established for the vigil of Pentecost; that fast is mentioned in the following prayers and preface.]

Another.

[Note: [Col. 0039C] This prayer occurs in Book I, no. 80, of the Sacramentary of Gelasius, on Pentecost Sunday. The Gregorian has it on the Saturday before Pentecost.]

Almighty and everlasting God, who willed the paschal mystery to be contained in the symbolism of fifty days, grant that the dispersion of the nations, brought about by the division of languages, may be gathered together by a heavenly gift into one confession of your name. Through [him], etc.

We implore your clemency, Lord, that you who always go before our evil merits in mercy may make us pleasing to you by expiation through pious acts and salutary fasts.

[Note: [Col. 0039D] More correctly: “may you make us pleasing.”]

Through [him], etc.

[Note: [Col. 0039D] This prayer is found in the Gelasian Sacramentary and in Gregory of Menard on the seventh day of the third week of Lent. In the Gregorian manuscripts edited by Muratori, however, and in the Roman Missal, it occurs on the Thursday after Passion Sunday.] Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the dignity of human nature, wounded by immoderation, may be restored through the discipline of medicinal restraint. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0039D] The same manuscripts of Muratori assign this prayer to the Saturday before Pentecost, at the descent to the font.] Merciful God, grant that we who, by violating the divine commandments, fell from the happiness of paradise may return to access to eternal blessedness through the keeping of your commandments. Through, etc.

Be present, Lord, with your faithful; be present with those who plead; and do not leave without earthly aids those whom you make participants in heavenly things. Through, etc.

May the working of the sacred gift cleanse and [Col. 0039C] strengthen us [Note: [Col. 0039D] *Renew* is a variant reading.] (*renew*), and join us to everlasting gifts. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. For, so that human nature may be restored to what it was made to be, in one and the same person you suitably assign to each its proper function. The body is nourished by food, the soul is fattened by fasting; unless supported by fitting nourishment, the limbs do not serve, and without self-restraint the mind’s command does not flourish. In this diversity of substance you govern us by such moderation that, since the one cannot endure without those things by which the other is refreshed, you command that they be taken in such proportion that both may be invigorated: so that nourishment for the flesh may at once not be lacking, whereby it may subsist, and observance may be present, whereby the mind may grow strong. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0039D] It is found in the Gelasian Sacramentary, book I, no. 79.] By the sacred heavenly things, Lord, may our vices be cleansed, so that we may always be made fit for your gifts. Through, etc.

Look graciously upon your suppliant people, Lord, and accompany with more generous kindness those who trust in your mercy; so that, since they cannot exist at all without you, they may be governed by your temporal benefits and advance toward eternal things. Through, etc.

## At Pentecost, as they come up from the font

### I

Grant us, ineffable and merciful God, that the adoption to which the Holy Spirit has summoned us together may possess nothing earthly in love and nothing diverse in confession. [Note: [Col. 0039D] This wording breathes the syntax of the Leonine collection.] Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0039D] This prayer also occurs in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal on the Monday after Pentecost.] In your mercy, Lord, sanctify these gifts, and, having received them through the offering of the spiritual sacrifice, perfect us as an eternal offering to you. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0040C] This entire preface occurs in the Gelasian Sacramentary for the vigil of Pentecost, book I, no. 78; in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal it extends to the word *poured out*.] Truly worthy. He who ascended above all the heavens and, seated at your right hand, poured out the promised Holy Spirit upon the children of adoption: therefore, rejoicing among your altars, Lord of hosts, we offer you sacrifices of praise, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0040C] A similar text, with some intervening words added, occurs in the Gelasian Sacramentary on the night of the Lord’s Supper, book I, no. 45, and is repeated at the vigil of Pentecost, no. 78. A not dissimilar text also occurs in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal at Easter and Pentecost.] Therefore, graciously receive this offering, which we present to you for those whom you have deigned to regenerate from water and the Holy Spirit, granting them the remission of all sins; and command that their names be written in the book of the living. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0040D] It is found in the Gelasian Sacramentary, book I, no. 78, and in the Gregorian Sacramentary of Menard.] In communion, and celebrating the most sacred day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit filled the apostles and the people of believers with the presence of his majesty; and also venerating the memory, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0040D] This blessing of milk and honey appears in Hittorp’s Roman Order on Holy Saturday, vol. I, p. 37. Tertullian, *On the Crown of the Soldier*, ch. 3, and book I *Against Marcion*, as well as St Jerome in his *Dialogue Against the Luciferians*, mention the use of milk and honey after baptism. See Martène, *On the Ancient Rites of the Church*, vol. I, book I, ch. 1, art. 15. Shortly afterward, the word *font* was wrongly inserted; it is rightly omitted in Hittorp’s Roman Order.] Bless, Lord, these creatures of yours, honey and milk (of the font); and give your servants to drink from this font of the water of everlasting life, which is the Spirit of truth, and nourish them with this milk and honey, just as you promised our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob [Note: [Col. 0040D] We have supplied the verb *you promised* from the Roman Order of Hittorp cited above.] that you would bring them into the promised land, a land flowing with milk and honey. Therefore join your servants, Lord, to the Holy Spirit, just as this honey and milk have been joined, by which the union of heavenly and earthly substance in Christ Jesus our Lord is signified. Through whom are all these things, etc.

### II. Another

[Note: [Col. 0041C] It is found in the Gelasian Sacramentary, book I, no. 79; in Muratori’s Gregorian Sacramentary on the Saturday before Pentecost; and in Pamelius, vol. I, p. 378.] Grant us, we ask, Lord, through the grace of the Holy Spirit, the new discipline of spiritual observance of your Paraclete, so that our minds, cleansed by sacred fasting, may be made more fit for all his gifts. Through, etc.

25 [Note: [Col. 0041C] This heading seems to have been inserted wrongly. What follows concerns the fast on the vigil of Pentecost, as will become clear from note 29 (immediately, no. d). Perhaps the prayer that follows, composed at a time when the fast of the Pentecost vigil had not yet been instituted, had previously been written under Wednesday, during the fast of the fourth month, for which it seems to have been composed by Leo. After the vigil fast was instituted, it was transferred from Wednesday to this vigil day, on which fasting began after the Easter season; and through the copyist’s carelessness the heading was transferred along with the prayer. Hence what follows is to be referred, together with the preceding prayer, to the same Mass, as they are joined in the Gelasian Sacramentary under the heading “At the vigil of Pentecost.”] **During the fast of the fourth month.**

[Note: [Col. 0041D] It is found in the Gelasian Sacramentary at the vigil of Pentecost, no. 79, and again under Wednesday, during the fast of the fourth month, no. 83; also in the Gregorian manuscripts and in the Roman Missal on Ash Wednesday. Some elements here come from Leo’s sermon 78, chapter 2, as does the following preface. The style and sentences certainly agree with sermons 78 and 79, composed by Leo during the fast of the fourth month.] Grant us, Lord, to begin the defenses of Christian warfare with holy fasts, so that, intending to fight against spiritual wickedness, we may be fortified by the aids of self-restraint. Through, etc.

God, by whose mysteries we are cleansed and nourished, grant that we may celebrate these temporal things in such a way that we may experience them as eternal for us. Through, etc.

### Presumption and Restoration of the First Man

[Col. 0041B] Truly worthy. He who, after that ineffably ordained union of the divine and human nature, foretold that the children of the Bridegroom could not fast until his departure—not wishing to burden the inexperienced minds of the little ones, who were to be imbued with heavenly instruction, with stricter disciplines, but reserving greater exercises for those who were making progress—dedicated to the better instructed, through the richer gift of the Holy Spirit, the first fruits of the fast that followed; so that, since after the creation of the first man desire had supplied the beginning of sin, after the restoration of the human race self-restraint might become the origin of virtues. Through, etc.

Almighty and everlasting God, who have brought the mystery of the Paschal solemnity to completion in the fullness of this present mystery [Note: [Col. 0041D] The words “of the present mystery” do not suit the days of the fast of the fourth month but the feast of Pentecost. Hence this other Mass has been wrongly joined to the preceding one under the heading “During the fast of the fourth month.”], grant, we ask, that, made children of your adoption, they may deserve the peace that our Lord Jesus Christ, coming to you, left behind. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0042D] It is found in the Gregorian Sacramentaries and in the Roman Missal on the Friday after Pentecost Sunday. For the institution and meaning of this prayer, see note 35 below.] Grant, we ask, merciful God, that your Church, gathered by the Holy Spirit, may in no way be disturbed by hostile attack. Through, etc.

Look graciously upon the offerings of your people, Lord; and, so that they may be made acceptable to you, let the saving coming of the Holy Spirit cleanse our consciences. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. On this day of the present solemnity, in which you perfect human substance, united from diverse superstition by the spirit of true religion. 26 Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0042C] It is read in the aforementioned Sacramentaries and in the Roman Missal on the Monday after Pentecost.] Be present, Lord, we ask, with your people, and defend from the fury of enemies those whom you have imbued with heavenly mysteries. Through, etc.

## XI. For Pentecost Sunday

Be present with our prayers, Lord, so that the adoption to which [you have summoned us] together, etc. [Note: [Col. 0042D] What follows is a repetition of the first prayer described above, for those coming up from the font.]

In your mercy, Lord, sanctify these gifts, we ask, etc. [Note: [Col. 0042D] The prayer given at the indicated place, likewise the second prayer, is repeated here.]

Truly worthy. May this confession of ours, Father of glory, always be pleasing to you, sent forth from the hearts of the children of promise; for we recognize that nothing more exalted was bestowed upon your Church at its beginnings than that the heralds of your Gospel should speak with the tongues of all believing peoples; so that both the sentence deserved by the once-proud construction of the Tower might be undone, and the variety of languages might not create difficulty for ecclesiastical edification [Note: [Col. 0042D] More pleasingly, “for the Church.”], but rather increase its unity. Through, etc.

### Against the enemies of the Catholic confession

[Note: [Col. 0042D] The Arian Vandals seem to be indicated here. In the year 455, they threatened Rome around the feast of Pentecost; for they entered the city three days after that feast, as we have shown in the preface to sermon 84. Leo may therefore be the author of this prayer and the following one, as well as of the two prayers described shortly before—“Grant, we ask” and “Be present, Lord”—in which divine help is requested against such enemies.]

### I

Hear our prayers, Lord, and just as you dispelled the profane darkness of the world by the light of the Holy Spirit, so defeat the enemies of the Roman name and the foes of the Catholic confession. Through, etc.

### Against emperors

God, who by the power of your Son and the Holy Spirit, destroying the treachery of the ancient ravager, gave us victory over captivity: grant, we ask, that those who plot to attack us may be crushed by the right hand of your power. Through, etc.

[Col. 0042C] [Note: [Col. 0042D] This prayer is found transferred in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal to the Wednesday after Pentecost.] Receive, we ask, Lord, the offering that has been presented; and graciously bring it about that what we perform in the mysteries we may celebrate through works of piety. Through, etc.

27 Truly worthy. Humbly imploring your clemency, we ask that, just as you opened for us the way to eternal security through the Passion of the Lord Jesus Christ and the illumination of the Holy Spirit, so you may also grant the tranquility of the present life, through which the quiet devotion that shares in so great a gift may advance, and the negligence [Note: [Col. 0042D] The printed editions had *and terror*, which is erroneous. Since these prayers concern the Vandals attacking Rome, as we noted in note 35 above, we believe that *and terror* should be read, with the letter *t* omitted—as commonly happens because of the occurrence of a similar letter at the end of the preceding word *and*. In this Vandal incursion, what negligence of the Romans is noted here we understand from Prosper’s *Chronicle* under the year 455. After recounting the death of the emperor Maximus, who had allowed everyone fleeing the city to depart, Prosper says that its defense was neglected because of this flight to such an extent that Genseric took Rome empty of every defense, while the holy bishop Leo met him outside the gates.] and terror [Col. 0043A] inflicted may be transferred to the increase of faith. Through, etc.

### II. Another

[Note: [Col. 0043C] The Gelasian Sacramentary assigns this prayer to Pentecost Sunday, book I, no. 80; the Gregorian manuscripts and the Roman Missal assign it to the Tuesday after Pentecost.] May the offering of the present gift purify us, we ask, Lord, so that it may make us worthy to participate in the sacred things. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0043D] Perhaps “Ferial prayers” should be read. Thus Blanchini.] **PRAYERS F.**

[Note: [Col. 0043D] In the Gelasian Sacramentary it is the Secret on Pentecost Sunday; in the Gregorian manuscripts and in the Roman Missal it occurs on the Tuesday after Pentecost.] May the Holy Spirit, we ask, Lord, prepare our minds for the divine sacraments, for he himself is the remission of all sins. Through, etc.

In communion, and celebrating the most sacred day of Pentecost, on which the apostles and the disciples of the apostles received the spiritual gifts of all charisms; and also venerating the memory, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0043D] In the Gelasian Sacramentary it is read in book I, no. 81, at vespers during the octave of Pentecost; in the Gregorian Sacramentary and the Roman Missal it is the first prayer for the aforementioned Tuesday. In all these Sacramentaries the ending is “may be protected from every adversity,” whereas ours has “from enemies,” perhaps because this prayer too looked toward the Vandal enemies threatening Rome, as we have said.] May the power of the Holy Spirit be present with us, Lord, we ask, which both mercifully purifies our hearts and protects us from every enemy. Through, etc.

## XII. During the fast of the fourth month

[Col. 0043B]

[Note: [Col. 0043D] It is now read in the Roman Missal on the Saturday before the First Sunday of Lent. This prayer is so distinctly Leonine that it contains Leo’s words from sermon 78, chapter 1. Compare note 2 on the same sermon (previous volume, col. 416, no. f).] Be present, Lord, with your suppliants, so that we may celebrate with devoted service this solemn fast, salutarily instituted for the healing of souls and bodies. Through, etc.

Grant, Lord our God, that by purity of mind we may overcome all the roarings of the impious, and that those who, trusting in their own strength, plot to afflict us may be subdued by us while we fast. Through, etc.

28 We offer you, Lord, what you have given to be consecrated in your name, humbly imploring that, just as you make it a sacrament for us, so you may grant that it become an everlasting remedy. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0044C] It is found in the Gelasian Sacramentary, book I, no. 83, and in the Gregorian Sacramentary of Menard under Wednesday of the fourth month. It attributes it to Leo, as we noted in note 8 on sermon 78 (previous volume, col. 417, no. c).] Truly worthy. For after those days of joy that we spent in honor of the Lord rising from the dead and ascending into heaven, and after receiving the gift of the Holy Spirit, these holy fasts were necessarily provided for us, so that, as we live in pure conduct, the things divinely bestowed upon the Church may remain. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0044C] It appears in the Gregorian manuscripts on 20 January, at the feast of St Fabian, and elsewhere. With the words “through the intercession of Blessed N., your martyr,” inserted, the Roman Missal frequently presents it in the common of one martyr, and elsewhere.] Refreshed by participation in the sacred gift, we ask, Lord our God, that we may experience the effect of the worship we perform. Through, etc.

[Col. 0044A] Be present, Lord, with your peoples who trust in your protection, and preserve them in perpetual protection as they humbly bow before your right hand. Through, etc.

May they receive help in the present life, we ask, Lord, and find everlasting grace. Through, etc.

## XIII. In June, on the eighth day before the Kalends of July: the feast of Saint John the Baptist

### I

[Note: [Col. 0044C] This prayer appears in the Gregorian Sacramentary, except for the opening words “of the heavenly powers.”] God of the heavenly powers, who allow us to celebrate each year the solemn feast of blessed John the Baptist, grant, we ask, that we may celebrate it with minds secure and, through the merit of his patronage, fully receive an increase of security. [Note: [Col. 0044D] *Their* was read incorrectly. The correction is supplied by the Gregorian examples.] Through, etc.

We gladly hasten to offer gifts, Lord, humbly imploring that, while honoring the glory of the Herald, we may receive the grace of the One announced. Through, etc.

29 [Note: [Col. 0044D] Compare this preface with Muratori’s Gregorian manuscript Ottobonianus for the vigil of St John the Baptist, p. 324, and with another manuscript of Menard; you will find similar texts.] Truly worthy. Presenting the solemn fast by which we anticipate the birthday of blessed John the Baptist [Note: [Col. 0044D] Thus our manuscript reads in Blanchini, as do two Gregorian manuscripts in Muratori. Muratori substituted *we celebrate* here because this Mass is placed under the feast of St John the Baptist. But under the heading “On the feast,” the compiler described together the Mass of the feast day and that of the vigil.]; his father, doubting that he would be born as the messenger of the Word of God, was deprived of the use of speech and received speech again when he was born; and while not believing what the angel promised, he became mute; but at the birth of the magnificent herald he became both speaker and prophet. His mother likewise, though barren, became fruitful not only in old age through childbirth, but also, so that she might receive the fruit of blessed Mary with attentive voice [Note: [Col. 0044D] “Blessing” is a variant reading inserted into the text.], she was filled with the Spirit of Divinity. He himself, born as the champion of the heavenly way, announced that the way should be prepared for the Lord; and, conceived and born late in his parents’ [Note: [Col. 0044D] The word *supreme* is also to be reckoned among the variants.] old age, he proclaimed the Redeemer who was to be brought forth in the final times. [Col. 0044C] Through, etc.

May the patronage granted by your saints, Lord, not abandon us, but protect our weakness both by their prayers and by their merits. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0044D] It is found in the Gregorian manuscripts.] Almighty and merciful God, who by your providence appointed blessed John the Baptist to prepare a perfect people for Christ the Lord: grant, we ask, that through the intercession of this Herald your household may both be stripped of all sins and [Note: [Col. 0045D] Either *and* is superfluous and *may find* should be read, or, with this word deleted, the words *may deserve to reach* should be substituted, as Muratori corrected it from the Gregorian Sacramentary.] find the one whom he prophesied. Through, etc.

### II. Another

[Note: [Col. 0045D] The Gregorian manuscripts place this prayer first in the Mass of St John the Baptist at the font.] Almighty and everlasting God, give our hearts that uprightness of your paths which the voice of blessed John the Baptist, crying out, taught. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0045D] This prayer is also read there in the first Mass of the same Forerunner, as well as in the Gelasian Sacramentary, book II, no. 26, and in the Roman Missal.] We heap your altars with gifts, Lord, celebrating with due honor the birth of the one who both sang that the Savior of the world was coming and showed that he had come. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. On this day of the present festivity, when that blessed Baptist John arose, revealing heavenly things before yet beholding earthly ones; preacher of eternal light before he experienced temporal light; witness of truth before sight; and prophet before birth; hidden in his mother’s womb and, with foreknowing exultation, announcing your Only-Begotten Son; and, though your Christ was not yet born, already his forerunner. Nor is it surprising that he showed your Son, Lord, when he was born, whom he recognized while still enclosed in the womb; and rightly no one among those born of women was found like him, because no human being at all was granted to act as an executor of Divinity before drawing the breath of human existence. It was sufficiently established how wondrous the One announced would be, since so remarkable a Herald appeared. And fittingly, in place of the ministry of the washing that he performed, he rendered service to the one who consecrated the mystery of perfect baptism; and, for the remission of sins to be bestowed upon mortals, he rightly rendered the service due to the one whom he had said came to take away the sin of the world. Therefore, with the angels, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0045D] This is the final prayer for completion in the Mass of the vigil of St John the Baptist in the aforementioned Gregorian manuscripts and in the Roman Missal. In the Gelasian manuscript, book II, no. 25, it is the second prayer of the vigil.] May the splendid prayer of blessed John the Baptist accompany us, Lord; and may he ask that the one whose coming he foretold favor us when appeased. Through, etc.

Stirred by great mysteries, may your people, Lord, [Note: [Col. 0046D] The following occurs in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal in the first prayer of the vigil.] walk along the way of salvation and peace, and, following the exhortations of the blessed Forerunner, may they reach in safety the one whom he foretold. Through, etc.

### III. Another

Almighty and everlasting God, who also, in the generation of blessed John, establish the confession of the people consecrated to you as something to be proclaimed: increase in us constancy of faith and piety, so that we may increasingly confess the excellence of the One announced, since the glory of the One announcing is so great. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0046D] This prayer appears in the Roman Missal on 16 September, in the commemoration of Saints Euphemia, Lucia, and Geminianus, martyrs, and also on 23 November for Saint Felicity.] Look graciously upon the vows of your people, Lord, and grant that those whose solemn feast you allow us to celebrate may make us rejoice through their intercessions. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. For deservedly no one among the children of men has been placed above this man, whom from his beginning to his end you consecrated with so many marks of goodness and so many splendors of spiritual gifts. For it was fitting that, visibly demonstrating the ineffable mystery of the Lord that he had foretold with a prophetic voice, he should appear more eminent than the other messengers of the Lord. Therefore, with the angels, etc.

Grant, we ask, Lord, that just as we pass from former things to new mysteries, so, having laid aside oldness, we may be renewed in sanctified minds. Through, etc.

Bless your people, we ask, Lord, and grant those who trust in the prayers of your saints to obtain what you have given them hope of. Through, etc.

### At the font

### IV. Another

[Note: [Col. 0046D] It is found in the Gelasian Sacramentary, book II, no. 26.] Almighty and everlasting God, who fulfilled the legal ordinances and the proclamations of the holy prophets in the days of your blessed servant John: grant that, when the figures of signs have ceased, truth itself may speak through its own manifestation. Through, etc.

Give, we ask, Lord, the light of understanding to your little ones, so that, with the grace of the present sacrifice succeeding the grace of the former sacrament, we may glory in the new without abusing the old. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. For all the ages are full of your mercy, which, as the appointed times of the law return, we also venerate in the festivity of this day; recognizing that it belonged to the great plan of your compassion that your holy John, whose birthday we celebrate to the glory of your name, should be born wondrous through so many gifts. Through, etc.

[Col. 0046C] Grant, Lord, our prayers, that, just as we have been transferred from former things to new mysteries, so, having laid aside oldness, we may be renewed in sanctified minds. Through, etc.

### V. Another

[Note: [Col. 0046D] It is found in the same Gelasian manuscript, in the same place, and in the Gregorian manuscripts and the Roman Missal on the very day of the Forerunner.] God, who have made the present day honorable for us in the birth of blessed John, give your peoples the grace of spiritual joys and direct the minds of all the faithful into the way of salvation and peace. Through, etc.

Almighty and everlasting God, who granted your faithful that he should arise who is greater than any born of women and should become the glorious Forerunner of your Only-Begotten Son: carry out the gift of your providence, so that what the testimony of the Herald has manifested may be fulfilled by the presence of the One announced. Through, etc.

[Col. 0046D] Having removed the shadows of fleshly victims, we bring before you, supreme Father, in humble service, a spiritual sacrifice, which by a wondrous and ineffable mystery is both always sacrificed and always offered; [Col. 0047A] and it is at once the offering of the devout and the reward of the one who gives the reward. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0047C] The Ambrosian Missal in Pamelius, vol. I, p. 393, presents this preface; it is also read among the ancient prefaces in vol. II, p. 587. The Gregorian manuscripts agree.] Truly worthy. On this day of the present festivity, when blessed John arose, who, not yet born, sensed the voice of the Mother of the Lord and, still enclosed in the womb, yearned through prophetic exultation for the coming of human salvation; who by his conception removed the barrenness of his mother and by his birth released his father’s tongue; and who alone among all the prophets showed the Redeemer of the world whom he foretold; and so that the nature of the waters might receive the effect of sacred purification, washed the very author of baptism in the sanctifying streams of the Jordan. Therefore, with the angels, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0047D] It is found in the Gregorian manuscripts and in the Roman Missal on the Wednesday after Passion Sunday.] Having received the blessing of the heavenly gift, we humbly beseech you, almighty God, that this same gift may always be for us both the source of sacrament and the cause of salvation. Through, etc.

Cover with your mercy those whom you make your own, Lord; and extend the assistance of all the saints over the weak, so that, with you inspiring them, they may run toward your promises and, with you guiding them, reach them. Through, etc.

## XIV. On the feast of Saints John and Paul

### I

Almighty and everlasting God, who perceive that we are not worthy, etc. [Note: [Col. 0047D] This prayer and the following prayers, together with the preface, are found above, in April, in Mass XXXIX of the common of martyrs.]

Help us, Lord, through the prayer of your saints, etc.

Truly worthy. He who not only the debt of the ancient death, etc.

### II. Another

May your people’s—be pleasing to you, Lord, etc. [Note: [Col. 0047D] Here the prayers and preface of Mass XL, inserted in the month of April, are repeated.]

Gifts dedicated to your name, Lord, etc.

Truly worthy. He who, for the greater triumph, etc.

### III. Another

Hear our prayers, Lord, and, so that they may be worthy, etc. [Note: [Col. 0047D] Here too the prayers of Mass XLI of the month of April are repeated.]

Truly worthy. For [it is] your work, Lord, etc.

33 ### IV. Another

Be present, Lord, we ask, with the vows of your Church; be present with its gifts; and let the intercession and merit of your saints make up what our conscience does not supply. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. For wondrous are the works of your justice and compassion, whether a human being, turning away from you, is subjected to the power of the devil, or, returning to you through your grace, not only escapes the right of the hostile ruler but, as we recognize in your saints, receives through your power dominion over him. Through, etc.

May your saints, Lord, plead for mercy, so that the sacraments we have received may bring us remedies both for the present life and for the future. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0047D] In the manuscript it is read as follows: “With the blessed martyrs supplicating, Lord, look graciously upon your faithful. They are yours, Lord, and subject to you; by your generosity may they receive your blessings, which they continually await with humility; but so that they may preserve the gifts bestowed, may they receive what they have humbly and justly hoped for.” Francis Pastor noted the following about this in Blanchini: “The Collect beginning ‘With the blessed martyrs supplicating,’ unless corrected, will trouble the reader’s ingenuity. Yet, if I am not mistaken, it is easily restored if we say that a single collect was confused by the copyist with a second and identical one, as may be inferred from the repeated word *may they receive*. We have retained his correction, which Muratori adopted. Pastor alone advised reading *one or the other* for *with humility*, either by supplying *with devotion* or by writing *humbly*, etc.] With the blessed martyrs supplicating, Lord, look graciously upon your faithful, so that they may preserve the gifts bestowed and receive what they have humbly and justly hoped for. Through, etc.

Those who are subject to you, Lord, may, by your generosity, receive your blessings, which they continually await with humble devotion. Through, etc.

### V. Another

[Note: [Col. 0048D] It is found in the Gelasian and Gregorian Sacramentaries and in the Roman Missal; from these the preposition *from* was supplied before “the blessed.”] We ask, almighty God, that the doubled joy of today’s festivity may welcome us, a joy that proceeds from the glorification of the blessed John and Paul, whom the same faith and passion made brothers. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0048D] It is read in the Gelasian and Gregorian Sacramentaries.] We place upon your altars, Lord, sacrifices of reconciliation, honoring your power in the sufferings of your saints and imploring forgiveness of sins for us through them. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. For although the precious merits of your righteous ones are present through your power wherever they are faithfully invoked, nevertheless in your powerful and merciful providence you granted us that you should crown not only the circuit of this city with the glorious sufferings of martyrs [Note: [Col. 0048D] The cemeteries are indicated here, in which the more ancient martyrs had been buried, whereas Saints John and Paul were entombed in the very heart of the city. Likewise, in the preface of the first Mass of St Xystus, on 8 August: “By whom [the martyrs] the circuit of this city was especially crowned.”], but also place the victorious bodies of Saints John and Paul in the very heart of the city, so that both an example of devout confession might confront those who looked within and without, and the help of magnificent blessing might not be lacking. Through, etc.

[Col. 0048C] 34 ### VI. Another

The honor of presenting gifts to you, Lord, urges us confidently to honor the blessed martyrs, because we believe that through them these gifts will benefit us. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. For that most devout saying of our Lord Jesus Christ shines forth, by which, coming to the world’s aid, he mercifully foretold: “Unless a grain of wheat, falling into the ground, dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit” (John 12:24). From this we see that abundant sowing has sprouted throughout the whole world, and that from the principal cross has come forth a glorious harvest of sufferings, because the Creator, pouring out his blood for impious servants, brought it about that sinful servants should eagerly die for their immaculate Lord. Therefore, etc.

### VII. Another

Lord, graciously regard the offering of our service, we ask; and, so that it may be commended through the prayers of your saints, forgive us. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. Set aflame by whose inspiration, the blessed martyrs hastened toward the glory of suffering, fearing not those who could kill the body, but him who could cast body and soul into Gehenna; and therefore savage persecution did not destroy them, but blessed confession exalted them. Through, etc.

### VIII. Another

Grant, Lord, through the prayers of your saints, that the gifts offered to your name may advance our sanctification. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. For we recognize it as the work of your power that your saints, according to the holy and heavenly teaching of our Lord Jesus Christ, loved holy souls by hating them, and guarded them rather by not preserving them; leaving us at the same time both this imitation of piety and this protection. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0049D] It is found in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal in the common of one martyr, and elsewhere.] Grant, we ask, Lord our God, that just as we rejoice for a time in the office of commemorating your saints, so we may rejoice forever in their presence. Through, etc.

35 May your people exult, Lord, supported by the aids of those who please you, through which they may both bring back sanctification and acquire help for their own weakness. Through, etc.

## XV. On the feast of the Apostles Peter and Paul

### I

[Note: [Col. 0049D] This prayer occurs in the Gelasian Sacramentary, book II, no. 31, and is nearly identical in the Gregorian Sacramentary and the Roman Missal.] God, who consecrated this day by the martyrdom of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, grant that your Church, spread throughout the whole world, may always be governed by their teaching, through whom it received the beginning of religion. Through, etc.

May the gifts of your people, Lord, become pleasing through the intercession of the blessed apostles, so that, since they are offered to your name for the sake of their triumphs, they may be made worthy through their merits. Through, etc.

Truly worthy. [Note: [Col. 0049D] This preface seems to be Leonine, as do several that follow for this feast.] In accordance with the ineffable ordinance of your promise, you grant through heavenly dispensation to the apostolic confession that, solidly founded upon your truth, no rights of deadly falsehood may prevail against it; and however great the multitude of those who err may be, they are children of your redemption, and the whole Church is reckoned among those who do not differ from the principal tradition of your elect. [Note: [Col. 0049D] In the following Mass XIV, where this preface is repeated, *dispensation* reads *condescension*.] [Note: [Col. 0049D] In that same Mass XIV: “Yet let them be children of your redemption, and let the whole Church be reckoned among them.”] [Note: [Col. 0049D] The word *principal* is absent in the cited Mass.] Through, etc.

## XVI. The joining of the offering of consecrated virgins

[Note: [Col. 0049D] Augustine, in Letter 3 to the presbyter Victorianus, and Ambrose, in his sermon to the fallen virgin, mention the offerings of virgins who had been consecrated to God at the sacred altar. From this we learn that their names were offered in writing and recited before the altar itself.]

[Col. 0049D] This offering also, O Lord, of the consecrated virgins [Col. 0050A] whose names, offered and recited before your holy altar, we ask you in your mercy to accept. For them we humbly beseech your majesty that they may preserve, with you as protector, the resolve of chastity which, with you as its author, they have professed. Through, etc.

## II. Another

[Note: [Col. 0050D] This prayer is read in Menard’s Gregorian Sacramentary, in the Roman Missal on the feast of the Conversion of Saint Paul, and elsewhere when a commemoration of this apostle is made.]

O Lord, we ask you, sanctify the gifts of your people through the prayers of your apostles, so that what is pleasing to you according to your institution may become even more pleasing through the patronage of those who implore you. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. And to praise you, O wondrous God, in your saints, in whom you have been greatly magnified; through them adorning the sacred body of your Only-Begotten, and establishing in them the foundations of your Church. Their most blessed Peter, the first-fruits of your grace and election, was summoned to the summit of apostolic dignity. By the secret revelation of yourself you taught him to confess you as the living God and Jesus Christ our Lord, so that, in recognizing the glory of your Only-Begotten, he would be hindered by no obstacle of flesh and blood. For this faith, the teacher of all believers, you appointed your confessor over the keys of heaven, so that he who had access to you through you might, through himself, open to others an entrance into your kingdom. To him also you joined the blessed apostle Paul, by a calling no less directed toward the salvation of the nations; prepared by great labors, your grace changed both his mind and his name. Therefore, celebrating today with devotion the day of this triumph, we offer you, O Lord, sacrifices of praise, with the angels, etc.

## III. Another

The blessed passion of your apostles, O Lord, we ask, may reconcile the offerings of your people; and what, owing to our merits, is (less) unsuitable [Note: [Col. 0050D] *Minus* is a variant reading, absent from the Sacramentary of Gelasius, where this prayer occurs. Immediately afterward the codex has *apta et placitae*. In the Gelasian text, *apta et placita* is more coherent. But we have corrected it to *aptae* and retained *placitae*, since these adjectives refer to the offerings.] to us, may become pleasing to you through the prayers of your righteous ones. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For you cause your Church, prevailing everywhere in your faithful, to stand firm in apostolic teachings, so that through those by whom it received the beginning of divine knowledge, it may through them receive the increase of the heavenly kingdom until the end of the age. Through, etc.

## IV. Another

May this gift, O Lord, we ask, be advanced on our behalf by apostolic intercession, so that what we vow through trembling service may, through their prayers, become for us a sacrament. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For you grant, O Lord, [Note: [Col. 0050D] The codex has *tribues* here, but in Mass VIII, where this preface is repeated, *tribuis* is better. There, instead of *subvertat*, one reads *commaculet*.] that no treacherous doctrine of infernal jurisdiction overturn the splendor of apostolic preaching, and that no betrayal of the truth obscure it. Through, etc.

[Col. 0050D] 37 [Note: [Col. 0050D] In the Sacramentaries of Gelasius and Gregory, and in the Roman Missal, apart from a few exceptions, a similar collect occurs on the feast of Saint Paul.]

Having received the sacraments, O Lord, with submissive heart we ask and beseech you that, through the intervention of the blessed apostles, what has been celebrated for their glory may profit us for healing. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0051D] You will find these sentences and formulas in the preface of the Gelasian Sacramentary for the octave of the apostles Peter and Paul, no. 36, and in the Gregorian and Roman Missal preface concerning the Apostles.]

Look with favor upon your flock, O good Shepherd; and through your apostles guard it with watchful protection, so that it may be governed by those same rulers whom you appointed as shepherds, vicars of your work. [Alternate: appointed.] [Note: [Col. 0051D] *Praefecisti* is a variant reading.] Through, etc.

## V. Another

Almighty and eternal God, who by an ineffable sacrament established the authority of apostolic primacy in the stronghold of the Roman name, from which evangelical truth would spread throughout all the kingdoms of the world: grant that what flowed throughout the earth through their preaching may be followed by the whole body of Christian devotion. Through, etc.

Grant, we ask, O Lord, that your Church may worthily rejoice in such great leaders and worthily follow with devout obedience [Col. 0051B] the teaching with which they instructed the flocks chosen for you through the sacred mysteries. [Note: [Col. 0051D] In a similar prayer of Mass XXII one finds *dilectos*.] Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For you chose not the kings and nobles of the world, not the eloquent or the rich, but the despised and poor, the uneducated and undistinguished, to whom you would reveal the power of your majesty and the mystery of your coeternal Son; so that it might be shown to be the work not of human ability but of divine gift; and so that what appeared greatest in the world might, without you, O God, be shown to be worthless, while every worthless thing might through you be taught to be sublime. Thus, by the ordering of your power, not the lowly would depend on the glorious, but the glorious on the lowly; and that once insignificant fisherman Peter, suddenly made an apostle, would not be subject to the powerful, but would rather enclose them in a saving net. Nor would anyone doubt that he, placed in secret blessedness, possessed the authority to forgive the sins of mortals, whose merit they could see reigning after death, venerated throughout the whole world.

You also glorify the blessed apostle Paul, O Lord, with a similar favor: cast down on earth, he is raised to heaven; deprived of bodily sight, he saw eternal light; and in one and the same manner your rebellious servant experienced both vengeance and grace. Through so felicitous a punishment, he deserved after his penalty to share in divine joys. [Note: [Col. 0051D] Supply “joys,” or something similar.] Through, etc.

## VI. Another

[Note: [Col. 0051D] It occurs in Muratori’s Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal on the octave of the holy apostles Peter and Paul. Immediately before *preces*, the codex inserts *quaesumus*; on the authority of that same codex, which repeats this prayer at no. 10 and concludes with the sole variation *apostolorum tuorum, quaesumus, precibus expientur*, we have placed the word before *precibus*.]

We offer you prayers and gifts, O Lord; and, that they may be worthy in your sight, we ask that they be aided by the prayers of your blessed apostles. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. You who rescue your Church, founded upon apostolic solidity, from the terror of the gates of hell, so that, standing firm in your truth, it may receive no fellowship with the faithless. Through, etc.

[Col. 0052A] ## VII. Another

## IX. Another

Almighty and eternal God, who made this day of the blessed, etc. [Note: [Col. 0052D] The following words are the same as in the first prayer of Mass I, except that here *moderamine* occurs in place of *magisterio*.]

Through, etc.

We offer you prayers and gifts, O Lord, etc. [Note: [Col. 0052D] See above, the collect of Mass VI.]

Truly it is worthy. You who by an ineffable sacrament established the authority of apostolic primacy in the stronghold of the Roman name, from which evangelical truth would spread throughout all the kingdoms of the world, so that what had flowed throughout the earth through their preaching might be followed by the whole body of Christian devotion; and so that, by a salutary abbreviation, those who had strayed from their path might be regarded as outsiders, while only those who in no way departed from the principal tradition might exist as children of the truth. Through, etc.

## After illness

## XI. Another

Truly it is worthy. You who mercifully chastise us with temporal afflictions because you do not wish us to suffer the loss of eternal things; and because security easily leads to a fall, you permit us, chastened by present evils, to advance toward divine things rather than to be led by worldly prosperity astray from the path of eternal blessedness. Through these benefits of your providence [Note: [Col. 0053D] *Beneficio* seems to be required. A little later, in Mass XVII, where this preface is read again, *multiplici solemnitate* occurs in place of *subdito corde*.], recognizing that we are instructed by apostolic teachings, we venerate with submissive heart the day of their glorious passion. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. You who establish your Church upon apostolic solidity, etc. [Note: [Col. 0053D] The preface of Mass VI is repeated here.]

Through, etc.

## XV. Another

[Note: [Col. 0054D] Here the prayer of Mass XXXVIII of April, from the Common of Martyrs, is recalled; the same is true of the following three collects, which you will find in that Mass.]

Almighty and eternal God, who, caring for our weakness, console us by the continual celebration of the saints: grant that, placed under such patrons, we may both be secured by continual protection and rejoice in salutary progress. Through, etc.

May our gifts be pleasing to you, O Lord; they have been instituted both by your commands and commended by the glorious feast of the saints. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. You who granted that, amid the darkness of worldly errors, the lights of manifold and blessed martyrdom should shine, so that before the eyes of the human race there might appear a wondrous change in their struggle: their persecutors are overcome by prevailing, while the slain prevail by dying; the memory and power of those raging men have vanished, while the death and name of those who died shine everywhere as precious; no insignia of royal power remain from the former, whereas the effect of the latter displays their virtue. What has become of both is perceived not only by faith but also visibly confirmed. Through, etc.

We ask you, O Lord our God, that, through the intervention of your saints, we may follow both in action and in understanding the sacred mysteries we celebrate. Through, etc.

Be present, O Lord, to your people who entreat you with the patronage of your saints, so that what they do not presume upon through confidence in themselves they may obtain through the merits of those who intercede. Through, etc.

Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0057C] It occurs in the Gelasian Sacramentary, book II, no. 33, among the prayers for Vespers. It is the prayer of the feast of all the apostles, to which the following preface also belongs. This feast was evidently celebrated within the octave of the apostles, as is clear from the cited Gelasian Sacramentary, no. 35. Concerning this feast of all the apostles, the venerable Cardinal Thomasius aptly noted, in the letter of Saint Jerome to Chromatius cited by Cassiodorus: “So that differing days may not seem to divide those whom the one dignity of the apostleship made sublime in heavenly glory.” Moreover, this prayer was transferred into Menard’s Gregorian Sacramentary and into the Roman Missal for the feast of All Saints on the first of November.]

[Note: [Col. 0057D] This collect for a fast was at times recited in the Mass of all the apostles, into which it was inserted; perhaps it indicates some extraordinary fast which was proclaimed either in the time of Leo as a thanksgiving after Rome had been liberated from the barbarians on Saint Peter’s day itself, as we saw in the note to Sermon 84, or for another reason during the octave of the holy apostles Peter and Paul when it coincided with the feast of all the apostles. In the Gelasian Sacramentary, however, this prayer is written for the vigil of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, book II, no. 29.]

We offer, O Lord, gifts for your glorification; may the prayer of those whose solemnity we celebrate make them pleasing to you for the sake of our fasts. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. You who established the foundations of the heavenly Jerusalem upon the holy mountains, and, solidified by the twelve stones of the apostles, display the choir of your Church through spiritual construction; showing us both that the mystery of the fourfold Gospel consists in the Trinity and that the fullness of the Trinity is contained in each of the Gospels; and likewise that, through your grace, teachers, advocates, and leaders of this dispensation were provided for our weakness, so that we might know that nothing more and nothing less was to be sought in the venerable sacrament of the sacred offering. Through, etc.

Sanctified, O Lord, by the saving mystery, we ask [Col. 0057C] that the prayer of those whose patronage you have granted us to be governed by may not fail on our behalf. Through, etc.

Grant your people, O Lord, we ask, the help of consolation; and grant relief to those laboring under prolonged calamities. Forgive their sins and guard their heart from iniquity, so that, since human weakness continually deserves offense, the continuing forgiveness of those who have fallen may come to their aid through the intercession of your saints. Through, etc.

## XXII. Another

[Note: [Col. 0058C] This prayer has some affinity with the one presented first in Mass I.]

Almighty and eternal God, who consecrated this day to the martyrdom of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul: grant that your Church, spread throughout the whole world, may follow with devout obedience the teaching of those through whom it received the beginning of its religion. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0058C] The prayer of Mass V is almost similar.]

Grant, we ask, O Lord, that your Church may worthily rejoice in such great leaders and steadfastly preserve the rule with which those same men, distinguishing between truth and falsehood, instructed the flocks chosen for you through the sacred mysteries. [Perhaps: “the beloved flocks.”] Through, etc.

P SP F E

## XXIII. Another

We commemorate the desired solemnities of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, O Lord. Grant, we ask, that we may be fortified by the prayer of those by whose authority we are governed. Through, etc.

We offer you gifts with rejoicing, O Lord, which we trust will profit us through the intercession of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul on whose natal days they are offered. [Note: [Col. 0058C] The codex reading is corrupt. Muratori, with Blanchini, thought it should be emended to *pro nobis intercedentibus*. We would prefer *eorum intercessionibus*.] Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. [Note: [Col. 0058D] Two features of this preface correspond exactly to Sermon 84 of Saint Leo, which was delivered on the octave of the holy apostles Peter and Paul. It mentions the incursion by which Rome was attacked by the Vandals and liberated through the feast and patronage of those same apostles; and it also hints at the Romans’ neglect of the cult of those saints. Both matters are explained more clearly in that sermon, as Acamius aptly observed on page 71. Hence this preface seems rightly attributable to the same author.]

You foresaw the troubles by which our city would suffer and placed within it the chief members of apostolic strength. But, O Rome, how happy you would be if you recognized your leaders [Note: [Col. 0058D] The codex has *Romana*, incorrectly.] and earnestly strove worthily to celebrate such great rulers! No enemies would attack you, no weapons at all would terrify you, if, truly and faithfully serving their teaching, you sought them with the resolve of Christian sincerity [the words in parentheses are a variant reading: “with a true and faithful purpose”]; for it is sufficiently clear to you what gifts they would confer upon those who deserve well, since they also protect sinners. Through, etc.

We ask you, almighty God, that we who are wearied by our offenses may be cleansed through the sacred mysteries; and that we who are afflicted by the just consequence of our iniquity may be protected by apostolic satisfactions. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0058D] It occurs in Saint Gregory’s Sacramentary at Vespers on the feast of Saint Peter. In Menard’s Gregorian codex and in the Roman Missal on 25 July, the feast of the apostle Saint James. Immediately afterward *gubernata* is a variant reading.]

Be for your people, O Lord, sanctifier and guardian, so that, fortified by apostolic protections, it may please you in its conduct and serve you securely. [“Governed” is a variant reading.] Through, etc.

## XXIV. Another

[Note: [Col. 0058D] It is read in Gelasius, book II, no. 31.]

By your generosity, O Lord, the light of the natal day of the blessed Peter and Paul has shone upon us. Grant, we ask, that the glory of today’s passion, just as it grants them everlasting magnificence, may also bring about for us perpetual protection. Through, etc.

A votive offering is brought to you, O Lord. We ask that, sanctified, it may likewise advance both the praise of your name, reverence for apostolic dignity, and our protection. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For your apostles, the blessed Peter and Paul, are now shown to reap in joy what they sowed in tears. Those who went forth while weeping, not terrified by death but sending forth precious seeds of blessed blood so that they might receive the fullness of passion, behold, now they come in the exultation of the whole Church, bringing the fruit of eternal victory and its rewards both for the present and for the future. Through, etc.

## XXV. Another

Through the prayers of your apostles, O Lord, sanctify the gifts of your people, etc. [Note: [Col. 0059D] What follows is as in the first prayer of Mass II.]

P F E SP

[Col. 0059B] [Note: [Col. 0059D] It occurs in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal on the feast of Saints Peter and Paul.]

May the offerings, O Lord, which we present to be consecrated to your name, be advanced by apostolic prayer, through which you grant us to be cleansed and defended. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. [Note: [Col. 0059D] It is related to the preface of Mass VI.] For it is your gift and the work of your power that your Church, founded upon apostolic solidity, may not be overcome by the terror of the gates of hell, and, standing firm in your truth, may receive no fellowship with the faithless. Through, etc.

Through the intercession of the blessed apostles, O Lord, we ask, etc. [Note: [Col. 0059D] You have this prayer above in Mass XVI.]

Be present, O Lord, to your faithful, etc. [Note: [Col. 0059D] This prayer also follows there.]

## XXVI. For Saint Paul

Through the apostolic patronage of the blessed Peter and Paul, O Lord, we ask you to protect us, and make those whose solemnity you have granted us to celebrate always secure guardians of us. [Col. 0059C] Through, etc.

We humbly bring gifts to your altars, O Lord, fearing as much on account of our own merits as we trust in the intercession of the blessed Peter and Paul, for whose solemnities they are offered. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. By whose providence and gifts it has been granted that the annual feast of the blessed Peter and Paul should be distinguished for us by their triumph: equal in the world’s veneration, first and least in the order of apostleship, yet sharers in grace and passion. The one is chief in confessing the faith; the other renowned in explaining it. The one, divinely inspired, proclaimed Christ, the Son of the living God; the other, made a chosen vessel, asserted that this same one was the Word, the Wisdom, and the Power of God. The one, establishing the primitive Church from the first-fruits of Israel, [Col. 0059D] the other, teacher and instructor of the nations to be called. Thus, by diverse dispensations gathering one family of Christ [Col. 0060A] together, although at different times, one recurring day united them forever in one crown. [Note: [Col. 0059D] See what we indicated concerning this sentence in the preface placed before this Sacramentary, no. 5.] Through, etc.

## XXVII. Another

Attend, O Most High, we pray, to the vows we render; and grant that they may become pleasing to you through the prayers of those for whose honor they are offered. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. [Note: [Col. 0059D] The preface is the same in the Gelasian Sacramentary, book II, no. 36, and nearly the same in the Gregorian Sacramentary on the feast of Saint Peter and in the Roman Missal from the Common of Apostles.]

We humbly beseech you not to abandon your flock, O eternal Shepherd, and to guard it continually through the blessed apostles, so that it may be directed by those same rulers whom you appointed as shepherds to preside as vicars of your work. Through, etc.

## XXVIII. Another

[Note: [Col. 0059D] In Gelasius, book II, no. 33.]

Rejoicing in the multiplication of the apostolic solemnity, we beseech your clemency, almighty God, that you grant us continually to be blessed by their confession and cherished by their patronage. Through, etc.

Grant, we ask, O Lord our God, both that we may venerate the natal days of your apostles with continual devotion and honor them more frequently at their own origins. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0059D] It occurs in Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal on the Thursday before Passion Sunday.]

O God, author and ruler of your people, drive away the sins by which they are attacked, so that they may always be pleasing to you and secure under your protection. Through, etc.

# XVII. In the Month of July. On the Sixth Day before the Ides of July

[Note: [Col. 0059D] This feast of the martyrs on the sixth day before the Ides of July, together with mention of their cemeteries, is similarly designated in the very ancient Bucherian Catalogue. They are the seven sons of Saint Felicity, known to have been buried in different cemeteries. None of these martyrs has a proper Mass; instead, common prayers for martyrs follow, since on each feast the prayers and prefaces were taken from the common formularies—unless Mass III perhaps belongs to them, whose preface mentions the martyred brothers and their mother.]

The natal day of the holy martyrs Felix and Philip, in the cemetery of Priscilla; Vitalis, Martial, and Alexander, in the cemetery of the Jordans; and Silanus, in the cemetery of Maximus on the Salarian Way; and Januarius, in the cemetery of Praetextatus on the Appian Way.

[Col. 0060C]

[Note: [Col. 0060D] The Gregorian Sacramentary and the Roman Missal present this same prayer, differing somewhat in wording but not in meaning, on 7 October, the feast of Pope Saint Mark.]

Hear our prayers, O Lord, and, with your saints interceding, graciously accept our prayers. Through, etc.

Receive our offerings graciously, Lord, and, through the intercession of your saints, kindly make them acceptable to your goodness. Through, etc.

Another. — Defend us, Lord, by the prayers and intercession of your blessed martyrs, so that, since we have no confidence in our own conscience, we may be protected by merits pleasing to you. Through, etc.
