Receive, we ask, Lord, the gifts of your servants, so that, through the intercession of your saints, they may benefit us both for the duty of pious devotion and for the effect of your sanctification [Col. 0060D]. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0060D] On the feast of Saint Hermes, 28 August, the Gregorian codices and the Roman Missal prefer this prayer.]

Filled, Lord, with heavenly blessing, grant, through the help of your saints [Col. 0061A], that what we undertake humbly we may experience as beneficial. Through, etc.

49 Another. — [Note: [Col. 0061D] It occurs in the Gregorian Sacramentaries and in the Roman Missal on 22 November, the feast of Saint Cecilia.] O God, who gladden us by the solemnity of your saints and rouse us to advancement by their imitation, grant that those whom we venerate in worship we may also follow as examples of a pious way of life, etc.

## During a Fast

### I

May the offerings of our fast be pleasing to you, we ask, Lord, because we then present them in worthy commemoration of your saints if we also follow their deeds. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For you are wonderful in all your saints, whom you have made illustrious by confessing your name and glorious through the suffering they endured for you. Therefore, just as they struggled by fasting and prayer so that they might obtain this victory [Col. 0061B], so we more appropriately celebrate their feasts by following what they practiced. Through, etc.

Filled, Lord, [Note: [Col. 0061D] The words “with the munificence of your grace” may perhaps seem redundant.] with the munificence of your grace and abundant blessing, and receiving heavenly gifts both for the services of our service and for the solemnity of the saints, we give you thanks. Through, etc.

Look with favor, Lord, upon your family as it supplicates you, so that what it asks under your inspiration it may obtain through the protection of the holy martyrs. Through, etc.

### II. Another

Our protector, look upon us, O God, and mercifully hear us as we humbly implore your mercy. Through, etc.

Look favorably upon the prayers of our humility, Lord; and do not allow us to fall into the pits and snares of the devil, whom you deign to fortify with such great protections of the holy martyrs [Col. 0061C]. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0061D] It occurs in the Roman Missal on 7 August, the feast of Saint Donatus the martyr.] Almighty and merciful God, who make us both participants in and ministers of your sacraments, grant, we ask, that in them we may advance both in sharing the faith and in worthy service. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. You graciously exercise us through the frequent festivals of the holy martyrs so that, by their blessed commemoration, you may lead us to steadfastness of faith and perseverance in devotion, establishing before us in their contemplation both an example of saving confession and the help of abundant protection; and inviting us to hope for the promise we shall receive through them, whose glory, though still hidden, you nevertheless already manifest even in this region of life. Through, etc.

[Col. 0061D] 50 [Note: [Col. 0061D] In the same Missal and in Menard it is read on 31 October, at the vigil of All Saints.] Lord our God, multiply your grace over us, and grant us to follow in holy confession the victory of those whose glorious struggles we celebrate. Through, etc.

Instruct your people, Lord, with spiritual disciplines, and make them devoted through consideration of those whose solemnities you grant them to venerate [Col. 0062A], and secure through their protection. Through, etc.

### III. Another

Grant us, almighty and merciful God, that the abundant victory of your holy martyrs, just as it gives them everlasting triumph, may likewise provide us with continual help. Through, etc.

Receive, we ask, Lord, the offerings of your people for the feast of the holy martyrs; and make us attend their feasts with a sincere heart. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For although you, Lord, are wonderful in the advancement of all your saints, yet in these we recognize your special gift: you made them brothers by the lot of their birth and kin by their magnificent suffering, so that there might be at once both the venerable glory of the mother and the flourishing offspring of the Church. [Note: [Col. 0062D] This codex inserts another particle, *et* (“and”), which seems more excessive here than before the word *veneranda* (“venerable”). Perhaps this is the proper Mass of the seven holy brothers, the sons of Saint Felicity, as we said in note 1 (Col. 59, n. j).] Through, etc.

Satisfied with the heavenly gift, we ask you, Lord our God, that these gifts may sanctify us through the prayers of your martyrs. Through, etc.

### IV. Another

[Note: [Col. 0062D] It occurs in the Gregorian Sacramentary of Menard and in the Roman Missal on 21 December, the feast of Saint Thomas the apostle.] Grant us, we ask, Lord, to glory in the sufferings of the holy martyrs, so that we may always trust in their protection and follow their faith with fitting devotion. Through, etc.

We offer you, Lord, gifts pleasing to you on the solemnities of your saints, humbly asking that what pertains to their glory may benefit us for forgiveness. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. You grant that your Church should advance through the commemoration of the holy martyrs, so that you may always gladden it by their festival, exercise it by the example of their pious confession, and protect it by prayer pleasing to you [Col. 0062C]. Through, etc.

Rejoicing in the exultation of your saints and satisfied by receiving your sacrament, we give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God. Through, etc.

### V. Another

Almighty, eternal God, who are everywhere wonderful in your saints, we ask your mercy [51], that just as you have bestowed eminent glory upon them, so you may make us assisted by their prayers in attaining your mercies. Through, etc.

Look favorably, Lord, upon the offerings of your people; and grant that what you have taught us to offer temporarily for the performance of the holy mysteries may advance us toward eternal salvation. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. He who not only endured the persecution of the ungodly for the salvation of the world [Col. 0062D], but also granted these gifts to his faithful, so that they might become sharers in him either through suffering or confession. Through, etc.

### VI. Another

Almighty, eternal God, who, among countless benefits, chiefly console us through the solemnities of your saints, grant, we ask [Col. 0063A], that both blessed remembrance and the worthy prayer of the righteous may urge us toward the practices of heavenly work and lead us to them. Through, etc.

Grant, we ask, Lord our God, that amid the adversities we endure as the due of our sins, the intercession of your martyrs may obtain for us what our confidence cannot obtain. Through, etc.

With the saints interceding, Lord, may our service please you, and may the services of our offerings become protections for the devoted. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For the venerable blood of the blessed martyrs, poured out in confession of your name [Note: [Col. 0063D] This codex has *simul et tua* (“at once also yours”) and shortly afterward *quo perficis* (“by which you perfect”), while omitting *ita* (“so”). We have corrected the text from Mass XXXII for several martyrs, described in April, where this preface is found, with only something altered at the end.] —just as it reveals your wonders, you who perfect strength in weakness—so it gives advancement to our efforts and provides help for those who are weak. Through, etc.

### VII. Another

Look, we ask, Lord, upon what we offer before the eyes of your majesty, so that, through the prayers of your saints, they may provide us both protection and healing. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For the whole body of the Church rejoices together in the glorification of its exalted members, and none of its weaker portions doubts that whatever excels among the parts of that great structure belongs also to its own dignity: for just as the lower members are joined to the higher, so the highest [Note: [Col. 0063D] The codex reads incorrectly; it should be “... affection.”] ought to impart the effect of unity to the humble. Through, etc.

## XVIII. Here begin the daily prayers and petitions

### I

Almighty, eternal God, who commanded us to inflict upon no one what we do not wish inflicted upon ourselves [Col. 0063C], grant, we ask, that we neither feign such things to others nor be deceived by the pretences of others. Through, etc.

O God, who rejoice in the faithful fellowship of the human race, grant, we ask, that we may offer free charity to everyone and that they may not attempt to repay good with evil. Through, etc.

Our offering is brought to you, Lord; grant, we ask, that it may be worthy of your sight and that it may proceed from the sincerity of our mind through your generosity. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0063D] In the margin of the codex it is noted: “The forgiving of a brother’s faults, and also the correcting of the restless, must not be omitted, as it is written.” This preface, together with the following Masses through the fifth (as Muratori observed in the preface, ch. 3, p. 23), was composed by some bishop who had suffered certain enemies and still feared them. He thinks that these matters may refer to the schism stirred up against Pope Damasus by Ursicinus in 367, or to that of Eulalius against Boniface I in 419. He also adds the accusations fabricated in 433 by Bassus, the former consul, against Xystus III, although he admits that they rest upon documents of doubtful reliability (he might have added), and which Father Coustant demonstrates to be spurious. More probably, however, we believe that the rebellion stirred up by clerics against Zosimus is indicated, mentioned in his Epistle 14, written in 418 in the same Coustant. Compare that editor’s notes and his account, no. 32, of the letters of the same pontiff which are no longer extant. Acamius interprets these passages as referring to the Manichaeans censured by Leo. We do not agree: for there is here no indication whatever of heresy or heretics, nor has anyone reported that they raised any persecution or spread calumnies against Leo. The style, indeed, assigns the authorship of this preface rather to Zosimus than to Leo.]

Truly it is worthy. You instruct us in spiritual disciplines and teach us continually to forgive the offenses of those who oppose us without falling into their snares; and so to overlook faults that, under the appearance of grace, we may avoid the malice of those who desire to harm us [Col. 0064A]. For you, Lord, sending us among wolves, wish us to remain simple in the likeness of doves and to become shrewd in the manner of serpents—not, certainly, so that we may harm anyone, but so that we may carefully avoid the deceit of others. Thus you command us to be gentle toward all that you likewise command us to correct the restless.

For it is one thing to pass over an insult, another to be watchful lest we be caught through improvident kindness. For your clemency also forgives our errors on this condition: that it again forbids us to err, lest we undergo worse things; and no one should judge that his offense has not been forgiven, or perhaps consider himself injured if the opportunity for further harm is rather taken away from him, since by this very act a great benefit is conferred upon such persons, so that they may unlearn being evil, or at least be prevented from sinning [Col. 0064B]. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0064D] You will find this prayer in the Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal on the Saturday before Low Sunday.]

Strengthened by the gift of our redemption [53], we ask, Lord, that true faith may always perfect in us this help of everlasting salvation. Through, etc.

Save your people, we ask, Lord, and pour out upon them the mercy of holy blessing, so that amid the assaults of human condition and diabolical deceit your forgiveness may continually come to the aid of those who labor. Through, etc.

### II. Another

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and, so that you may graciously rescue us from our enemies, first cleanse us kindly from ways displeasing to you. For without doubt you will defend those whom you see conforming to your commands. Through, etc.

O God, who wished prudent and sincere concord to dwell in the hearts of your people, grant us to maintain the measure of lawful love, so that those who dissent from the purity of just peace may nevertheless find nothing in us that they rightly ought to tear apart [Col. 0064C]. Through, etc.

Grant us, we ask, Lord, to despise earthly things and love heavenly things, so that through these sacred rites we may deserve both to be cleansed from passing desires and to begin to cling to things everlasting. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0064D] In the codex this marginal note is attached: “Prayer should be made for fraternal love.” At the end one might perhaps read “and those whom we love.”]

Truly it is worthy. You do not abandon the rational creature, but show both how it can please you and how it can obtain what it asks; commanding that those who chiefly venerate you with their whole heart should consequently love all human beings as themselves, as sharers in our nature [Col. 0065A]. Then we prove true affection toward them when, just as we desire to be cleansed from faults, we also desire this for those whom we love. By fulfilling the whole law without difficulty through these two commands, may we receive present goods and eternal ones. Through, etc.

Grant us, Lord, we ask, to pursue what is right and avoid what is harmful, so that the holy things we receive may benefit us not for judgment but rather for healing. Through, etc.

Watch over your servants, Lord, we ask, and, freed from earthly errors, make them advance in the disciplines of your virtues; and let them be strengthened by temporal helps in such a way that they may rejoice more in everlasting things. Through, etc.

### III. Another

[Note: [Col. 0065D] The Gregorian codices place this prayer among the daily prayers; the Roman Missal places it among the common prayers against persecutors of the Church. In them, for *adversantibus* (“those opposing”) there is *adversitatibus* (“adversities”); in the Missal, *et erroribus* (“and errors”) is added. In the Gelasian codex it is found in Book III, no. 67, against judges who act wickedly.]

Graciously receive the voices of your Church, Lord [Col. 0065B], so that, once all those opposing us have been destroyed, it may serve you in secure freedom [54]. Through, etc.

Grant, Lord, we ask, that, subject to you with our whole heart, we may reject the impulses of swelling wills. Through, etc.

Receive, we ask, Lord, the sacrifices of our devotion; and through glorious sacrifices purify hearts that are subject to you. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0065D] A marginal note in the codex reads: “He rebukes the wicked, but also prays for them.”]

Truly it is worthy. By whose inspiration blessed Paul the apostle clearly showed the Church, saying, “Providing what is good not only before God but also before human beings” (Romans 12:17), that there is no way at all for us to hide our evil deeds in this life: we do not escape your notice inwardly, nor do we avoid human observation outwardly. Nothing, therefore, benefits those who do not see their own disgrace and defects and, because they do not see themselves, suppose that they are not seen by others.

For when the same Apostle cries out, “Look at what is according to outward appearance” (2 Corinthians 10:7), how can those who, as it is written, “by their smooth speech deceive the hearts of the innocent” (Romans 16:18), and who, as the Gospel says, seek Christ in a chamber, trust that they can conceal themselves? They openly and plainly reveal what they pursue both in words and in deeds.

Nor does it support or protect them that, in order to maintain their authority, they pore over the divine books, since through these they rather both proclaim and condemn their wicked ways, unaware that the punishment of divine judgment is already coming upon them: they are handed over to a reprobate mind, to do what is not fitting (Romans 1:28) [Note: [Col. 0065D] The following six words, which the codex places after the word “suitable,” were moved here by Muratori in his edition for clarity, at Blanchini’s suggestion; we have judged that they should not be altered.]

Therefore, avoiding such people in action and pitying them with the only affection with which we ought to pity them; and therefore, etc.

Grant, we ask, Lord our God, that through this sacrament of your wisdom we may live with circumspect moderation. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0065D] Nearly the same prayer occurs in the Roman Missal on 15 June, the feast of Saints Vitus and Modestus.]

Grant your Church, Lord, not to think arrogantly but to advance in humility pleasing to you, so that, despising the insolent and desiring all that is mature, it may practice free charity. Through, etc.

### IV. Another

Release us, Lord, we ask, from our iniquities, and, so that we may deserve to receive your gifts, make us love justice. Through, etc.

Grant us, Lord our God, both to venerate you with our whole mind and to love all human beings with rational affection. Through, etc.

Consecrate, we ask, Lord, what you have commanded to be dedicated to your name from earthly fruits, so that you may make our service pleasing to you and establish for us the sacrament of everlasting salvation [Col. 0066B]. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0065D] In the margin of the codex it is noted: “Prayer should be made for those who are ill-disposed.”]

Truly it is worthy. Making your faithful concordant by a mutual law, you bound them together by such a covenant of true peace that no one would attempt to inflict upon another what he would not wish inflicted upon himself; and that the good things he would desire to be granted for his own advantage by a fellow member of nature, he himself might also provide to that person. Thus, while through mutual kindness they discover themselves to be common in each individual matter, there would be one mind of all, loving itself [Note: [Col. 0066D] The codex inserts *fieret* (“would become”), which is a variant reading for *esset* (“would be”) and should preferably be deleted.] . Through, etc.

Satisfied with heavenly participation, we give you thanks, Lord our God, and beseech you that it may be perpetual for us. Through, etc.

May your faithful people always rejoice in your benefits, Lord, we ask, so that, instructed and ordered by you, they may please you in their way of life and beneficially obtain what they seek in their prayers [Col. 0066C]. Through, etc.

### V. Another

[Note: [Col. 0066D] This prayer is found in the Gelasian and Gregorian Sacramentaries under the title “In Contention.” The Roman Missal presents much of it among the common prayers requesting humility.]

Almighty, eternal God, who resist the proud and grant grace to the humble, grant, we ask, that we may not provoke your indignation by being elated, but, having subjected ourselves, may receive the gifts of your forgiveness. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0066D] A marginal note in the manuscript reads: “Against those who tear apart or flatter.”]

We humbly implore your majesty [Note: [Col. 0066D] The following words through “to love” are found in the Gregorian and Gelasian codices, in the Mass against slanderers.] that you neither allow us to be terrified by unjust attacks nor entangled in crafty flatteries; but rather grant us to love those who rebuke truthfully rather than those who flatter deceitfully. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0066D] A marginal note in the manuscript reads: “For the double-hearted.”]

We offer you, Lord, a gift which condemns those who receive it with a divided heart, but justifies those who receive it with a sincere mind. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0066D] Another marginal note reads: “Prayer should be made for persecutors.”]

Truly it is worthy. You wish us to be perfect in both devotion and justice, so that kindness joined to our caution may not be lacking, nor indiscriminate ease of access steal upon our charity [Col. 0067A]. For you command us to pray for our enemies, to plead for those who slander us, and not to cease obtaining your mercy for those who persecute us—not, certainly, so that they may persist in the same wickedness, since that would be to wish evil rather than to ask for what is salutary, but so that, freed from these iniquities, they may turn toward what is moderate and sound.

For when, Lord, you teach us that we ought to wish good conduct for ourselves, then we truly love our neighbors as ourselves if we desire for them what we wish to have ourselves. Through, etc.

Refreshed, Lord, by the taste of the sacred gift, we ask that it may not become punishment for us who partake of it, but may benefit us for forgiveness as we receive it faithfully. Through, etc.

56 Trusting in your protection, Lord, may your devoted family obtain the blessing it has humbly sought [Col. 0067B], so that, secure under your protection, it may neither lack temporal assistance nor fail to be fitted for eternal goods. Through, etc.

### VI. Another

[Note: [Col. 0067D] This prayer is read in Muratori’s Gregorian codices under the heading “Prayers in Time of War.”]

Almighty and merciful God, we ask you to make us quiet amid the turmoil of wars, because you will provide us with every good if you grant peace of mind and body. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0067D] It occurs in the Roman Missal among the common prayers against persecutors and evil-doers.]

Our protector, look upon us, O God, and defend us from dread of our enemies, so that, once all disturbance has been removed, we may serve you with minds set free. Through, etc.

Receive, Lord, the gifts of your family; through them, we ask, be appeased both toward our errors and work in us the sanctification of your redemption. Through, etc.

[Col. 0067C] [Note: [Col. 0067D] The codex attaches this marginal note: “It is completely certain that enemies harass us because of our sins; hence God must be entreated with greater insistence.”]

Truly it is worthy. We acknowledge, Lord our God, we acknowledge—as you long ago testified through the prophetic voice—that it belongs to the deserts of sinners that what has been acquired through the labor of your servants should be seized before our eyes by foreign hands [Note: [Col. 0067D] Although the style of this preface seems Leonine, it indicates the plundering of the city of Rome and the devastation of the fields carried out by the Vandals under Leo the Great in 453, rather than the event that occurred under Pope Innocent I in 410.] and that what you grant to be produced by laboring servants should be allowed to be consumed by enemies.

Prostrate in supplication with our whole heart, we implore you to grant forgiveness for our past sins and, through continual mercy, to protect us from every assault of mortality. For we do not doubt that your defense will be present when you graciously drive away from us those whom we have offended. Through, etc.

Strengthened by the nourishment of the most holy body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, we humbly ask you, God, that through this unique remedy you both cleanse us from the contagion of all sins and guard us from the assault of every danger [Col. 0067D]. Through, etc.

[Col. 0068A] Have mercy, Lord, on the Church that entreats you [Note: [Col. 0067D] The codex reads “and of those bowing down.” We have retained Blanchini’s emendation, adopted by Muratori, from whom the subsequently added word “of things” also comes.], and look favorably upon those who bow their hearts before you, so that those whom you allow to share in divine things you may neither permit to become liable to sins nor allow to be crushed by adversities. Through, etc.

### VII. Another

[Note: [Col. 0068D] It occurs in the Roman Missal on Tuesday after the fourth Sunday of Lent.]

Have mercy, Lord, on your people, and graciously grant relief to those laboring under continual tribulations. Through, etc.

57 [Note: [Col. 0068D] This prayer is read in the Gregorian Sacramentary among the daily prayers.] May the voice of the Church crying out ascend to the ears of your mercy, Lord, we ask, so that, having received forgiveness of sins, it may become devoted through your working and secure through your protection. Through, etc.

Sanctify the gifts dedicated to your name, Lord, we ask, so that they may provide us both the sacrament and the advancement of eternal life. Through, etc.

[Col. 0068B] [Note: [Col. 0068D] A marginal note in the codex reads: “In dangers or prosperity, thanks should be given to God.”]

Truly it is worthy. For amid all the dangers of the world, the sole prosperity is not to depart from you, since no adversities strike those who trust in your mercy, but rather exercise them toward salvation. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0068D] In the Gregorian Sacramentary codices, according to Muratori, it is read on the Thirteenth Sunday after Pentecost; according to Menard, on the Fourteenth; in the Roman Missal, on the Twelfth.] May participation in your holy mystery give us life, Lord, we ask, and grant us at once purification and protection. Through, etc.

Assist your people, Lord, and grant those subject to you with their whole heart the effect of a worthy way of life, because you will fill them with every good if you make them pleasing to you. Through, etc.

### VIII. Another

[Note: [Col. 0068D] Thus begins the collect for sins in Muratori’s Gregorian manuscripts, and it continues through “and those,” after which its style changes somewhat.]

Having forgiven us, Lord, release us from all sins, we ask, and overcome those who strive to attack us. Through, etc.

Restrain, Lord, we ask, the mouth of those speaking iniquity [Note: [Col. 0068D] The codex incorrectly reads *Deus* (“God”) instead of *os* (“mouth”)], and refute those who endeavor to accuse us [Col. 0068C]. Through, etc.

We ask, Lord our God, that through this commerce of heavenly life, avoiding the snares of falsehood, we may be directed toward your truth by the divinely granted road and path. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0068D] In the margin of the manuscript: “Prayer should be made for those who tear others apart.”]

Truly it is worthy. You deign to instruct your servants so that the senseless attack of the proud may not so much harass us as the pity of those who tear others apart move us. For just as we ought to take care lest we be attacked truthfully, so we ought to mourn the destruction of those who have strayed from the truth. We ask that, by humbly praying, we may be able either to help them through correction or to acquire for ourselves the fruit of devotion. Through, etc.

Those whom you have refreshed with the heavenly mystery, graciously release from their own sins and those of others [Col. 0068D], so that, with minds purified by the divine gift, we may enjoy it. Through, etc.

[Col. 0069A] [Note: [Col. 0069D] It is found in Muratori’s Gregorian Sacramentary among the daily prayers, vol. II, p. 256.]

Extend your right hand, we ask, Lord, to your people seeking mercy, through which it may avoid human errors, receive the consolations of mortal life, and attain everlasting joys. Through, etc.

### IX. Another

58 Release us, Lord, we ask, from the debts of our sins, and, so that you may graciously rescue us from all evils, absolve our iniquities, for which they are justly repaid [Note: [Col. 0069D] Thus the codex reads, and correctly, since the phrase refers to the evils.]. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0069D] It occurs in the Gelasian Sacramentary, Book III, no. 58.] Crush, we ask, Lord, the enemies of your people, and cleanse us from our sins, by whose merit they dominate us; so that, when you have poured into our minds a purity pleasing to you, you may also grant us peace. Through, etc.

Receive, Lord, we ask, the unique sacrifice that is always both rendered and owed to your majesty. Through, etc.

[Col. 0069B] May this sacrifice be acceptable to your name, Lord, when it is offered, so that it may continually become something required. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. You heal us by chastising and kindly instruct us by restoring us, since you prefer those corrected to be saved rather than those neglected to perish. Through, etc.

We humbly ask you, Lord our God, that we who have received the substance of the heavenly table may reach eternal life [Note: [Col. 0069D] The codex incorrectly reads *pertineamus* (“may we belong”); we accept Blanchini’s emendation.]. Through, etc.

They are your people, Lord, who await the ministry of our voice. We ask your mercy: grant to those requesting what is salutary whatever the confidence of the supplicant lacks, through your grace, which has no need of our good works. Through, etc.

### X. Another

Be present, Lord, to your suppliants [Col. 0069C], and graciously protect those who hope in your mercy with heavenly aid. Through, etc.

Look upon us, Lord, we ask, as we seek the help of your devotion. Grant forgiveness to the guilty, so that, having been appeased, you may help us who are afflicted. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0069D] Thus in the Gregorian Sacramentary and the Roman Missal on Tuesday after the Second Sunday of Lent.]

Work your sanctification in us through these mysteries, Lord, having been appeased, so that it may cleanse us from earthly faults and lead us to heavenly gifts. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0070D] In the margin of the codex: “Concerning justice.”]

Truly it is worthy. By purifying our minds you justify us, and by justifying us you make us capable of immortality. Through, etc.

May we be filled, Lord, with the grace of the sacred gift, and may what we touch with sweet veneration in bodily taste be felt as sweeter in our minds. Through, etc.

Have mercy and look upon the prayers of your family [59] [Col. 0069D], and pursue, sustain, and surround with care those who are subject to you with their whole heart, so that, trusting in you as their guide, they may be entangled in no evils and may be filled with every good. Through, etc.

### XI. Another

Almighty, eternal God, whose ways are always mercy and truth, grant, we ask [Col. 0070A], that we who are nourished by your clemency may also grow through an increase of religion. Through, etc.

Grant us, we ask, Lord, to handle your mysteries worthily, so that we may respond with services suitable to your mercies and ask with greater confidence for what we ought to hope. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0070D] A marginal note in the codex reads: “While prosperity overflows, heavenly instruction should be sought.”]

Truly it is worthy. Desiring your goodness with all our prayers, grant that, having received prosperity in human affairs, we may rejoice in earthly consolations only to such an extent that we do not cease seeking heavenly joys, but that whatever joy is spent upon temporal things may advance everlasting instruction. Through, etc.

We ask, Lord our God, that you sustain by protections those whom you refresh with the sacraments, and feed with everlasting [Note: [Col. 0070D] *Divinis* (“divine”) is a variant reading.] things those whom you nourish with temporal benefits. Through, etc.

[Col. 0070B] Pursue your Church, Lord, with unceasing mercy, so that, established amid the storms of the world, it may both breathe again in present joy and receive the splendor of eternal blessedness. Through, etc.

### XII. Another

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and, trusting in apostolic intercessions, may we be disturbed neither by the threats of those who oppose us nor by any assault. Through, etc.

Assist our times, Lord, so that, with your right hand protecting us everywhere, both the integrity of religion and the security of the Roman name may stand restored. Through, etc.

We humbly ask, Lord, that the offering presented in trembling service may not be judged according to our merits, but that what has been instituted by you may be sanctified for us by your gracious acceptance of those who offer it [Col. 0070C]. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0070D] In the margin of the codex: “It admonishes us to be more ready to pray.”]

Truly it is worthy. Even its austerity heals us, since it restrains the inclination to sin, makes the human mind more ready to pray to you, causes tranquility to return more gratefully after adversities, and amid these things trains tested faith for its reward. Through, etc.

Release us from every evil, and graciously grant that what we ask to be forgiven us, we also may forgive our neighbors. Through, etc.

We ask, Lord our God, that what you wished to be for us a pledge of immortality you may grant to become an aid toward eternal salvation [60]. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0070D] It is found in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal on Ash Wednesday.]

Look favorably, Lord, having been appeased, upon those who bow before your majesty, so that those refreshed by the divine gift may always be protected by heavenly helps. Through, etc.

### XIII. Another

Grant us, we ask, Lord our God, always to rejoice in devotion to you, because happiness is perpetual and complete if we continually serve the author of every good. Through, etc.

We ask, almighty God, that the prosperity bestowed upon us may not lead to neglect of your worship, but [Note: [Col. 0069D] [ [Col. 0069D] This note appears at the foot of column 69, but the callout letter (d) has not been printed in the text.] Marginal note in the codex: “After illness.”] [Col. 0071A] may always kindle us more fervently toward thanksgiving to you. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0071D] The same prayer occurs in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Missal on Tuesday after Passion Sunday.]

We bring you, Lord, sacrificial offerings, signifying through temporal consolation that we should not despair of the promises made for eternity. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0071D] In the margin of the codex: “Thanks are attributed to the inspiration of God’s grace.”]

Truly it is worthy. For just as your clemency not only bestows benefits upon the undeserving but also inspires in us the disposition by which we may give thanks, so it is fitting that, since we cannot adequately fulfill your praises, we should at least utter them without ceasing; so that, although we can never repay them sufficiently, we may never cease rendering them. Through, etc.

Rejoicing in the celebration of the annual observance, may we enjoy the full effects of those whose practices we follow. Through, etc.

[Col. 0071B] May your Church, Lord, be filled with heavenly grace and grow; and, cleansed from every vice, may it receive an increase of everlasting redemption, so that what it venerates in its members through the abundant extension of time it may receive through the generosity of spiritual gifts. Through, etc.

### XIV. Another

Almighty, eternal God, turn our minds, we ask, toward works pleasing to you, so that your correction may not be a greater cause of punishment for the negligent, but may become paternal instruction for those who have been corrected. Through, etc.

O God, who placed all the ordinances of the sacred law in love of you and of one’s neighbor, graciously grant us the ability to carry out these commandments, since no one can excuse himself by saying that what is contained in such brevity and commanded with such fairness is impossible. Through, etc.

[Col. 0071C] Almighty, eternal God, who grant the offerings to be presented to your name and ascribe what has been offered to the devotion of our service, we ask your mercy: grant that what you provide as the source of merit may advance us toward reward. Through, etc.

61 [Note: [Col. 0071D] Marginal note: “He restrains the insolent.”]

Truly it is worthy. You, just and kind, instruct our changeability toward things unchanging, so that you neither abandon our frailty nor fail to restrain the insolent; and, instructed together by a pious way of life and heavenly sacraments, we may use passing goods now in such a way that we may already be able to cling to everlasting things. Through, etc.

Hear, O God, our prayer; and do not allow your holy gifts, which we have received, to come to us for judgment, but rather let them bring a remedy of immeasurable propitiation. Through, etc.

[Col. 0071D] Look graciously, Lord, upon your people, and cleanse from every evil of body and mind those whom you make sharers in your gift, so that, when harmful disturbance has ceased, they may always offer you free service. Through, etc.

XV. Another.

Grant us, Lord, we ask, your grace, by which we may be good, [Col. 0072A] and grant that we may pursue it with appropriate zeal. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0071D] “We ask,” previously placed above, is found here superfluously in the manuscript.]

O God, whom our injustice continually offends, grant us the practice of upright conduct, through which we may also obtain forgiveness. Through, etc.

May the offering, Lord, which is to be consecrated, purify us and likewise make us worthy through its ministry and participation. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0071D] In the margin of the codex: “God is to be entreated concerning the vices to which we are subject.”]

Truly worthy. You govern our care in such a way that external results proceed from the quality of what is within. For we shall be afflicted by no outward miseries if we restrain the vices of our souls; nor will one who has opposed shameful desires be subject to visible disgrace; no disturbance will prevail outwardly if we act with a sincere heart; we shall be subject to no enemies if we maintain inward peace. Thus, just as we are harmed by no one more than by ourselves, so all harmful things will yield if we first conquer ourselves. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0072D] Thus the codex. Muratori has “we shall conquer,” following an emendation indicated by Blanchini; but this does not seem necessary.]

May the heavenly medicine of your sacrament grant us, Lord, we ask, health of mind and body, so that, invigorated by its operation, we may receive both present and eternal assistance. Through, etc.

May what your Church suppliantly asks obtain the help of your blessing, receive indulgence, be instructed in good works, breathe again through the consolation of temporal necessities, reach everlasting joys, and take possession of eternal things. Through, etc.

62 XVI. Another.

Help us, O God our Savior, and to those to whom you grant the inclination to pray to you, grant also the effect of your propitiation. Through, etc.

[Col. 0072C] As we perform your mysteries with the service that is owed, we humbly ask you that what we offer to the honor of your majesty may profit us for salvation. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0072D] A marginal note in the codex recommends not trusting in riches, but only in the grace of God.]

Truly worthy. We first perceive the beginning of your propitiation chiefly in this: that you graciously pour into the minds of your own people the desire to supplicate you with their whole hearts, and to trust not in human resources but in your power. We recognize your unfailing grace when you grant us either to persevere in this devotion or, concerning the benefits we have received, to glory not in ourselves but in your name. Through, etc.

Having been satisfied with the saving gift, we beseech your mercy, Lord: by this same sacrament through which you strengthen us temporally, make us participants in eternal life. Through, etc.

Be of assistance, Lord, to your servants, and remain continually propitious to those who trust in your goodness, so that, with you protecting them, they may avoid present dangers, and, with you granting them, receive future joys. Through, etc.

XVII. Another.

[Note: [Col. 0072D] This prayer occurs in the Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal on Thursday before the First Sunday of Lent. In the cited codices, however, it is repeated among the prayers for sins.]

Spare, Lord, spare your people, so that, chastened by deserved scourges, they may breathe again in your mercy. Through, etc.

Hear, Lord, your people, and what they lack in the merits of those who supplicate, may your grace, always going before us, generously provide. Through, etc.

We bring our offerings of service to your altars, Lord; receive them graciously, and may they make our service acceptable to you and effect the sacrament of our redemption. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0073D] The codex reads “receiving,” and below “may it make.”]

Truly worthy. We must never cease praising you, for you provide necessary help amid distress, and in prosperity you cause us to give you thanks. The more you make us mindful of your benefit, the more you reconcile your gifts to us. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0073D] The Roman Missal presents this prayer on the Twenty-Third Sunday after Pentecost and among the common prayers against persecutors of the Church.]

We ask, Lord our God, that those whom you grant to rejoice in divine participation, you may not allow to be subjected to human dangers. Through, etc.

Almighty and eternal God, instructor and ruler of the faithful people, preserve the gifts of your grace in the household acquired through the sacrament of your name, so that the good things it has received through you as their author may be preserved under your protection, [Col. 0073B] 63 or, alternatively, may increase more abundantly through your generosity. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0073D] The adverb was inserted into the text in another form in the codex, indicating a variant reading.]

XVIII. Another.

Almighty and eternal God, grant us to retain your will with faithful minds and to express it through holy conduct, so that, once your Church has been purified from profane vanities, it may not profess one thing in words and practice another in action. Through, etc.

Hear us, Lord our God, and distinguish the hearts of your faithful from the wickednesses of the world, so that those who confess the Lord with their voice may not fall back into diabolical servitude. Through, etc.

That the offering of your people may be pleasing to you, cleanse us, we ask, from every contagion of perversity, [Col. 0073C] and do not allow those whom you promise will come to the rewards of your truth to cling to false joys. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0073D] Thus the codex. Muratori has “those whom,” instead.]

Truly worthy. You desire that your Church be cleansed from diabolical pretence, and, so that you may distinguish the sincere from the feigned, you command that the fruits of intentions be understood from the quality of their works, not counting as belonging to you those whom you see either concealing what is yours or doing what is contrary to it. Therefore we bless you, Lord, and praise you with the service that is owed. Through, etc.

Be present to us, almighty and merciful God, and do not allow the sacraments that we have received to be violated either by our offenses or by the sins of others. Through, etc.

Look graciously upon your flock, good Shepherd, and do not allow the sheep whom you redeemed with your precious blood to be torn apart by the devil’s attack. Through, etc.

[Col. 0073D] XIX. Another.

[Note: [Col. 0073D] This prayer is related to that of the Gregorian codices in Muratori’s morning prayers, but in Menardus it appears among the daily prayers.]

Receive, we ask, Lord, our prayers, and look graciously upon the holy petitions of those who cry out to you. Through, etc.

[Col. 0074A] [Note: [Col. 0073D] The same codices place this among the prayers for sins.]

Hear, Lord, we ask, the groaning of your people, and may the offense of those who sin not have greater force before you than your mercy, which is always granted to the tears of those who supplicate. Through, etc.

Graciously regard the sacrifice to be celebrated for you, Lord; may it both cleanse us from the vices of our condition and render us acceptable to your name. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0073D] A marginal note in the codex: “It is obtained more slowly so that the prayer of the one asking may persevere.”]

Truly worthy. You delay the requests of those who ask for this reason: so that they may also make progress through the very length of their supplication; and by granting what is requested more slowly, you are known to bestow upon the minds of your faithful an increase of devotion. Through, etc.

We humbly beseech your majesty that, just as you feed us with the nourishment of the most holy Body and Blood, so you may make us participants in the divine nature. Through, etc.

[Col. 0074B] May those who trust in your protection and glory in you alone as their Protector be fortified by heavenly defenses, Lord, we ask, and may they always be cherished by your help. Through, etc.

XX. Another.

Hear, Lord, our prayers, and gladden us by your swift propitiation. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0074D] The Gregorian codices of Muratori present this prayer among the morning or evening prayers.]

Look upon your suppliants, Lord, we ask, and graciously grant us both indulgence and joy. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0074D] It is found in the same manuscripts in the Masses for weekdays.]

Receive graciously, Lord, the offerings presented, and by sanctifying them make them salutary for us, we ask. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0074D] Marginal note: “Concerning false brothers.” This Leonine preface seems to describe the corrupt conduct of certain false brothers. We do not wish to conjecture who they were.]

Truly worthy. Instructing us in every respect through heavenly disciplines, and showing us how we should distinguish false brothers from your faithful [Note: “Showing” is redundant owing to a variant reading, unless one prefers to read “you show,” and below “declaring,” as Blanchini observed.], you declare through the voice of your Only-Begotten: “You will know them by their fruits” (Matthew 7:20). These are the ones puffed up with the sense of their flesh and not holding fast to the Head. These are the ones who, thinking earthly thoughts, despise the words of those who pray to you, because, being animal and carnal, they do not grasp in their foolish minds the things that belong to the Spirit of God.

[Note: [Col. 0074D] Marginal note: “Concerning the disdainful.” And after a little: “Concerning the deceitful.”]

These are the reprobate concerning the faith, who, not knowing what they are saying or about what they are making assertions, have often tried, and continue to try, to overturn others. These are the deceitful workers who enter in order to spy out the freedom of the Church, which it has in Christ, so that they may reduce it with themselves to shameful slavery. These are the ones who penetrate houses and take captive little women burdened with sins, devouring not only the resources of widows but also those of married women.

[Note: [Col. 0074D] Another marginal note in the codex: “Devourers of widows and married women.”]

These men no longer even seek to appear just, nor are they at least outwardly either whitened or washed; but openly, having trampled on shame, they even glory in their depraved conduct. Gathering filthiness at home and abroad, they are not so much filled with the bones of the dead as they themselves are dead.

[Col. 0075A] The Gospel judgment fittingly cries out against them: “If the light that is in you is darkness, how great is that darkness” (Matthew 6:23)? For since the things that are seen in them are obscure and black with the disgrace of an evil reputation, it is sufficiently evident that they conduct in secret things that would also be shameful to speak of.

These men not only deter those who come to your grace by their own foulness, but, even among the brothers established within, for whom Christ died, they place the stumbling block of their perversity. You command us to beware of such people, saying through your Apostle: “Separate yourselves from every brother who walks disorderly” (2 Thessalonians 3:6). And you command us to do those things which, when all your truly faithful see them, will cause them to praise and magnify you, the heavenly Father, from whom every perfect and excellent gift of rational conscience and good reputation descends. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0075D] In the Gelasian Sacramentary this is read on Saturday after the Third Sunday of Lent; in the Gregorian codices of Muratori and in the Roman Missal, on Thursday after Passion Sunday.]

What we have received with the mouth, Lord, may we grasp with the mind; and may what is a temporal gift become for us an everlasting remedy. Through, etc.

Look upon your male and female servants, Lord, we ask, to whom you have granted hope in you; and grant them both to ask for what pleases you and rather grant what they ask. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0075D] Perhaps one should read “graciously.”]

XXI. Another.

[Note: [Col. 0075D] The Gregorian codices of Muratori place this among the morning prayers up to the words “overcome them.”]

Grant us, Lord, forgiveness of our offenses, and overcome those who strive to attack us, because no stealthy assault of the devil will harm those established under your protection. Through, etc.

God, protector of those who hope in you, hear our prayers and have mercy on us, so that, invigorated in body and mind, we may always cling to your service. Through, etc.

[Col. 0075C] We humbly ask you, God, that the offerings we bring may confer upon us both the grace of devotion and salvation. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0075D] In the margin: “Right conduct.”]

Truly worthy. Just as you never cease instructing the children of your Church, so you never cease helping them, so that they may know what ought rightly to be done and receive the ability to carry it out. Through, etc.

Receiving heavenly gifts, we give thanks to you, holy Father, almighty and eternal God. Through, etc.

Protect your faithful, Lord, and accompany with perpetual salvation those whom you have graciously chosen to enliven with spiritual food. Through, etc.

66 XXII. Another.

Increase your faith in us, Lord, we ask, in your mercy, because you will not deny the helps of your goodness to those to whom you have granted firmness in believing in you. Through, etc.

Grant us, Lord, we ask, to trust in you with our whole mind, because just as you always oppose the proud who presume upon their own strength, so you do not abandon those who glory in your mercy. Through, etc.

Offering gifts to you, Lord, we ask that you may deign both to cleanse us from all sins and protect us from every adversity. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0075D] It is noted in the margin of the codex: “Thanks are to be given for God’s works.”]

Truly worthy. Since every good work is known to be begun by you, and to be brought to completion by this very perseverance in supplication that you grant us, we are certain that we can obtain what we ask. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0075D] It is found in the Roman Missal on the Fifth Sunday after Easter and [Col. 0076D] at the Vigil of the Ascension.]

Grant us, Lord, satisfied with the power of the heavenly table, both to desire what is right and to receive what we have desired. Through, etc.

Be, we ask, Lord, the defense and guardian of your people; you, the sustainer and ruler of the present life; you, the bestower of the eternal one. Through, etc.

[Col. 0076B] XXIII. Another.

Watch over us, your servants, Lord, we ask, so that, abstaining from every sin, we may serve you with a ready will. Through, etc.

May the offering of your people be pleasing to you, Lord, we ask, through which it may both return sanctification and obtain what it devoutly requests. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0076D] Marginal note: “God is present to the humble in all their works.”]

Truly worthy. In your mercy you regard our frailty, and you grant us both the mind to supplicate and your gifts to those who supplicate. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0076D] It is read on Passion Sunday both in the Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal.]

Be present to us, Lord our God, and defend with perpetual protections those whom you have refreshed with your mysteries. Through, etc.

Kindly enlighten your household, Lord, and strengthen it through the abundance of your blessing, so that it may deserve to have you as its guide in all things and as its guardian. Through, etc.

XXIV. Another.

Almighty and merciful [Col. 0076C] God, to whose eternal blessedness one ascends not through the frailty of the flesh but through the eagerness of the mind, make us always aspire, with you inspiring us, to the courts of the heavenly city, and enter them confidently through your indulgence. Through, etc.

O God, who, although you need no gifts, yourself bestow every gift upon us, receive graciously what you have wished us to offer you from your gifts; not only reckoning as our devotion what belongs to you, but also leading us through these things to the heavenly kingdoms. Through, etc.

P S F E

We give you thanks and render praises to you, Lord, who have strengthened us through communion with the Body and Blood of your most beloved Son, our Lord; humbly beseeching your mercy, [Note: [Col. 0076D] The following words are inserted into the prayer after Communion for the living and the dead, which is likewise read in the Lenten Masses.] that this sacrament of yours, Lord, may not be guilt for our punishment, but may become a saving intercession for forgiveness. [Col. 0076D]

XXV. Another.

Protect, we ask, Lord, [Note: [Col. 0076D] From this and similar passages, in which Roman rulers or princes are addressed in the plural, some have inferred that this Sacramentary was compiled when two emperors were reigning, one in the East and the other in the West. How weak this reasoning is is shown by the fact that the same formulas are also read in some prayers of Book III of the Gelasian Sacramentary. Thus, no. 59, prayer 3: “Be propitious to the princes of the Roman Empire”; no. 6, prayer 2: “Be propitious to the princes of the Roman name,” and in the secret: “Defend the rulers of the Roman Empire”; and no. 61, prayer 1: “Be present to the rulers of the Roman Empire,” etc. These prayers could indeed have been composed under two emperors; but that they could also have been incorporated into the Sacramentary after the last emperor of the West had been removed is demonstrated by the Sacramentary of Gelasius, during whose pontificate one emperor ruled in the East.] the rulers of the Roman name everywhere, so that, with them conquering through your power, the peace of your people may arise secure. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0077D] Among the daily prayers, this is the last in the Gregorian codices of Muratori.]

Extend your mercy to us, Lord, so that what we seek in our petitions we may attain through conduct pleasing to you. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0077D] The Sacramentary of Gregory of Menardus and the Roman Missal place this prayer on Thursday after Easter.]

Hear, Lord, our prayers, so that the most holy exchange of our redemption may both bring us the help of present life and procure everlasting joys. Through, etc.

P F C SP

Having been satisfied with the blessing of your sacraments, we ask, Lord, that through them we may always be cleansed from vices and guarded against dangers.

[Note: [Col. 0077D] The codex reads “that we may be avoided,” incorrectly.]

Be present, we ask, Lord, to your people, so that what they have received faithfully they may preserve, with you protecting them, both in mind and body.

[Note: [Col. 0077D] The codex reads “they received,” which could be retained, since “people,” meaning a multitude, may take the plural number. But below “may preserve” would then coherently be required. Immediately afterward, instead of “together,” the codex has “for itself.”]

[Col. 0077B] 68 XXVI. Another.

Hear, Lord, our prayers, and, so that you may continually accompany us with your gifts, make us always devoted to your majesty. Through, etc.

Almighty and eternal God, who graciously anticipate us, undeserving as we are, with your gifts, grant that, while giving you thanks, we may also become worthy. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0077D] The Gregorian codices of Muratori insert this prayer after the last Mass of the weekdays.]

We offer you, Lord, the gifts that you have given, so that they may both testify to the help of your creation concerning our mortality and bring about for us the remedy of immortality. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0077D] A marginal note in the manuscript: “The fountain of life is to be loved with the whole heart,” that is, Christ our Redeemer. This preface is found in the Gregorian codices in the eighteenth week after Pentecost.]

Truly worthy. Although you do not need our praise, the devotion of your servants is nevertheless pleasing to you; our proclamations do not increase you, but they benefit us for salvation. For just as passing by the fountain of life is a cause of dying, so continually overflowing from that same fountain is the effect of living without end. Through, etc.

As we partake of heavenly gifts, Lord, we rejoice that protection is present to us, and amid these things that pass away, we trust in those that will remain.

[Note: [Col. 0078C] The codex reads “and of those things that will remain.” The passage has been emended in printed editions, but not entirely satisfactorily. “Those things that are to remain” would be preferable.]

Protect your servants, Lord; nourish them with bodily support; and, feeding them with spiritual nourishment, make them secure from every enemy. Through, etc.

XXVII. Another.

Turn us, Lord, by the help of your propitiation, so that chastisement appropriately applied to sinners may become a saving correction. Through, etc.

[Col. 0078A] Regard our prayers, Lord, we ask, and insert the presence of your majesty into these gifts, so that what is carried out through our service may be formed by you rather than by us. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0078D] In the margin of the codex: “Whatever we do, as ministers of faith, must unquestionably be attributed to the grace of God.”]

Truly worthy. We first perceive your propitiation in this: when we desire to seek what is pleasing to you and salutary for us. Since without you we can neither will, nor do, nor complete anything right, whatever we carry out appropriately is unquestionably of grace. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0078D] In the Gelasian Sacramentary and in Gregory according to Menardus, this is read on Tuesday after the Fourth Sunday of Lent; in the Gregorian codices according to Muratori and in the Roman Missal, on Thursday.]

We ask, Lord, that you not allow the heavenly gifts received to come to judgment, since you have provided them as a remedy for your faithful. Through, etc.

Be present, Lord, to the peoples who have touched the sacred gifts, so that those who trust in you as their protector may be afflicted by no dangers. Through, etc.

XXVIII. Another.

We proclaim your magnificence, Lord, humbly imploring that you, who have delivered us from impending dangers, may also graciously absolve us from sins, so that you may grant us greater benefits and make us obey your commandments. Through, etc.

We bring gifts to your name, Lord, with thanksgiving, for you grant us, after freeing us from hostile enemies, to receive the paschal sacrament with a secure mind.

[Note: [Col. 0078D] If the Huns are indicated here, as Acamius thinks in part II, § 9, the peace made with them by Leo would have to be placed before Easter. Why we should hesitate on this point you will understand from note 7 (Col. 281, note a) in Quesnel’s first dissertation on the year 452. Immediately afterward, “peaceful” is a variant reading.]

Truly worthy. We beseech your majesty with all our faculties that you may drive away our vices just as you extinguish the deadly enemies of our bodies; and do not allow us to endure inward captivity, which you have removed outwardly. Rather, so that you may disperse every harmful thing and continually bestow prosperity, complete in us always the avoidance of what is wrong and the love of what is just. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0078D] In the margin: “God is to be entreated to drive vices away from us.” Then, in the codex, “of bodies” is incorrectly written as “of which.”]

We do not keep silent about your praises, Lord, because, having freed us from the evils we deserved, you grant us to celebrate your goodness with joy. Through, etc.

Grant your faithful, we ask, Lord, to persevere always in sacred worship, so that those who are made worthy by your mercy may become still more worthy through the service of piety. Through, etc.

XXIX. Another.

[Note: [Col. 0078D] It is found in Book III of the Gelasian Sacramentary, no. 8; in the Gregorian manuscripts of Muratori, on the Thirteenth Sunday after Pentecost; but in the Roman Missal, on the Twelfth Sunday.]

Almighty and merciful God, from whose gift it comes that you are served worthily and laudably by your faithful, grant that we may run without stumbling toward your promises. Through, etc.

Receive, we ask, Lord, the gifts that we offer from benefits bestowed by you, and may what you grant to our devotion to be effected temporarily become for us the reward of eternal redemption. Through, etc.

P F E SP

XXX. Another.

[Note: [Col. 0079D] It is found almost identically in the Gregorian codices among the series of prayers for sins, and in the Roman Missal among the common prayers for any tribulation.]

Do not despise us, Lord, we ask, when we cry out in affliction, but graciously come swiftly to the aid of those who labor. Through, etc.

Look upon us, almighty and merciful God, and, being propitious, absolve us from every tribulation. Through, etc.

Send, Lord, we ask, the Holy Spirit, who may make these present gifts your sacrament for us and purify our hearts for receiving it. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0079D] A marginal note in the codex: “Adversities are driven away, prosperity is supplied.”]

Truly worthy. When we proclaim you without ceasing, neither adversities prevail nor prosperity is denied. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0079D] In the Roman Missal this is read on the Eighth Sunday after Pentecost and on the feast of Saint Valentine, February 14. In the Gregorian Sacramentary of Muratori, on the Ninth Sunday after Pentecost; in Menardus, on Saint Valentine’s Day.]

May the heavenly mystery be for us the restoration of mind and body, Lord, and may we experience the effect of that whose celebration we perform. Through, etc.

May your people, Lord, receive the gift of holy blessing, through which they may both avoid every harmful thing and obtain what they desire. Through, etc.

XXXI. Another.

[Note: [Col. 0079D] It exists in Book III of the Gelasian codex, no. 37, in the Gregorian and Pamelian manuscripts, and in the Roman Missal, for the repelling of storms.]

Almighty and eternal God, who both heal us by chastising and preserve us by forgiving, grant your suppliants that we may rejoice in the consolation of the desired tranquility and use the gift of your peace for the purpose of correction. Through, etc.

Receive our prayers graciously, Lord, and make those whom you grant to serve the heavenly mysteries purified from earthly contagions. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0079D] In the margin of the codex: “Christ redeemed us from sins or dangers.”]

Truly worthy. Through him you rescue us from sins, deliver us from dangers, and lead us to everlasting joys. Through, etc.

We ask, Lord our God, that, having received the holy gifts from your table, we may take the heavenly gifts not for judgment but for everlasting protection. Through, etc.

Look graciously upon your people, Lord, and sustain those who belong to your mercy with present and eternal benefits.

[Note: [Col. 0079D] “Present” and then “future” are variant readings.]

[Col. 0079D] Morning prayers, or prayers for evening.

[Note: [Col. 0080D] It is found in Book III of the Gelasian Sacramentary, no. 84.]

O God, who distinguish day and night, distinguish our deeds from the darkness of obscurity, so that, always meditating on what is holy, we may continually live in your light. Through, etc.

[Col. 0080A] Grant our prayers, Lord, and guard with vigilant protection those who cling to your service. Through, etc.

Lord our God, refresh us, wearied by the labor of the day, with the rest of sleep, so that, assisted by the necessary help of frailty, we may be devoted to you both in body and in mind. Through, etc.

Be propitious, Lord, to those who seek your mercy, and everywhere defend the condition of the Roman name.

[Note: [Col. 0080D] The words enclosed in parentheses were inserted into the text by the compiler from a variant reading.]

(Alternatively: “and everywhere protect the sovereignty of the Roman name.”)

So that the perpetual peace and safety of your peoples may be able to flourish. Through, etc.

Again, for evening.

[Col. 0080B] [Note: [Col. 0080D] This is the penultimate of the evening prayers in the Gregorian manuscripts of Muratori.]

We ask, Lord our God, that you sustain the troubles of the day with the rest of night, so that, as the necessary alternation of the seasons succeeds, our weakness may be restored. Through, etc.

Hear us, almighty and eternal God, and, lest human frailty fail beneath unending labors, refresh us by the very variation of changing things. Through, etc.

Be present to our prayers, Lord, and protect us by day and night, so that through whatever alternations of the seasons occur, we may always be strengthened by your unchangeableness.

[Note: [Col. 0080D] The codex reads “may be established,” incorrectly.]

XXXII. Another.

Look graciously, Lord, we ask, upon the affliction of your people, and do not allow our sins to prevail for our destruction; rather, may your abundant mercy prevail beforehand for our salvation.

[Note: [Col. 0080D] “But” is superfluous.]

[Col. 0080C] Regard graciously, Lord, we ask, the gifts that we present at your altars, so that what is offered through our frailty may be consecrated by your power. Through, etc.

P F C

[Note: [Col. 0080D] It is found in the Roman Missal among the common prayers for any need.]

We have received the gifts of the sacred mystery, Lord, humbly beseeching that what you commanded us to do in your remembrance may profit us for the help of our weakness. Through, etc.

Rule the hearts of your faithful, Lord, we ask; and, so that they may receive your good things through your generosity, first grant—or, alternatively, make—their wills good. Through, etc.

XXXIII. Another.

[Note: [Col. 0080D] The Gelasian codex presents this in Book III, no. 9. In the Gregorian codices of Muratori, on the Fourteenth Sunday after Pentecost; in Menardus, on the Fifteenth; in the Roman Missal, on the Thirteenth.]

Almighty and eternal God, grant us an increase of faith, hope, and charity; and, so that we may deserve to attain what you promise, make us love what you command. Through, etc.

O God, who have placed the fullness of the commandments in love of you and of one’s neighbor, graciously bestow this grace upon us: since we offend in many things, may your charity abound in us, through which sins are cleansed. Through, etc.

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, look graciously upon the offerings of your household, so that these acts of devout service may sanctify both the rulers and those who are ruled. Through, etc.

O God, who desire your faithful to reach true innocence, make us, through your indulgence, participants in that holiness which is found harmful neither to itself nor adverse to anyone. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0081D] The codex reads “your faithful.” From the context, however, one must read either “your faithful,” or add “hearts” or “minds.”]

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, give your servants this affection of charity, so that, following your example, they may be moved to return good for evil, and may desire the correction of their enemies more than rejoicing in vengeance. Through, etc.

Be propitious to the vows of those who supplicate, and, having received the offerings and prayers of your people, turn all our hearts toward you. Through, etc.

P F E. Here begin the daytime prayers with the necessary headings.

XXXIV.

Almighty and eternal God, assist the Roman princes, so that, strengthened by your power, all hostility may prevail neither by force nor by deceit. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0081D] It is found among the daily prayers in the codices of Muratori.]

Be propitious, we ask, Lord, to our times, so that both Roman security and Christian devotion may be directed by your gift. Through, etc.

We humbly beseech you, Lord, that through these gifts of the unique sacrifice there may be provided for us both the abolition of sins and your sanctification. Through, etc.

[Col. 0081C] Truly worthy. You allow our enemies, even in ineffable ways, to rise up in insult against you, so that, since we do not deserve to be avenged for our deeds upon their savagery, while injuries done to you are brought to vengeance, provision is nevertheless made for us, wicked as we are; and at the same time, by these things being bestowed on sinners, you admonish us how much you can bestow upon those who are corrected. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0081D] Marginal note: “Concerning hostile insult, which is established as pertaining to the correction of the faithful.”]

May your glorious mercy purify us, Lord, we ask, and make us worthy to receive its benefits. Through, etc.

May unconquerable defense by your power fortify your faithful people, we ask, and may it receive what is holy through your heavenly dispensation, so that, always devoted to you with pious affection, it may both be freed from hostile enemies and persevere continually in your grace. Through, etc.

XXXV. Another.

Grant us, Lord, we ask, constancy in supplicating you without ceasing, so that those whom you do not abandon when they are subjected to tribulation you may cherish more abundantly as they continually entreat your majesty. Through, etc.

Grant, we ask, Lord, that, purified by this offering, we may receive both confidence in prayer and the grace of obtaining what is just—or, alternatively, what is good. Through, etc.

During a fast.

Truly worthy. And the more earnestly may we do what we strive to perform according to our measure, insofar as we hope to obtain through fasts and prayers what we ask; especially since the testimony of what has been granted gives hope concerning what is to be requested. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0081D] The codex reads “may we be purified.”]

Lord our God, who alone foresee and bestow what is salutary, grant, we ask, that you may always give our minds the desire to ask for your mercy, and graciously regard what is useful to us. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0081D] The codex reads “effect.”]

May the Lord our God hear you, and in his goodness look upon each person crying out according to his need; may he graciously provide the consolations that human frailty requests; may he turn away the sins that oppose us; and may he always grant what will benefit both your bodies and your minds. Through, etc.

XXXVI. Another.

Lord our God, we ask, graciously grant that your Church may continually grow both in religion and in peace. Through, etc.

74 May the offering presented reconcile us to your mercy, Lord, and likewise profit both our protection and our salvation. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0081D] A note in the margin of the codex: “Everything adverse pertains to correction.”]

Truly worthy. You not only grant forgiveness to us when we sin, but also powerfully oppose our enemies; and those whom we deserve, by our evil deeds, to endure, you drive away through your magnificent goodness, so that you compel us to worship your reverence both through fear and lead us to it through love. Through, etc.

[Col. 0082C] [Note: [Col. 0082D] It is found in the Gregorian manuscripts of Muratori and in the Roman Missal on the First Sunday after Pentecost.]

Filled with such great gifts, Lord, that we may always receive saving gifts, grant, we ask, that we may never cease praising you. Through, etc.

Stretch out your right hand, we ask, Lord, to the people who pray; and to those to whom you graciously grant the inclination to supplicate, provide help in your favor, so that, trusting with you as guide, they may avoid every evil and grasp everything that is good. Through, etc.

### XXXVII. Another

Almighty and eternal God, graciously grant to your Church that, once deadly (variant: sacrilegious) entertainments have been cut away, it may rejoice instead in delight in your eternity. Through, etc.

[Note: At [Col. 0082D], *sacrilegis* is a variant reading inserted into the text by the first hand; the second has *sacrilegiis*, a variant reading of the noun *oblectationibus* (“entertainments”). This Mass seems to be directed against spectacles, as the words of the preface imply: “when crimes are performed or sung about.” This agrees with what St Leo discusses in Sermon 84, chapter 1.]

Help us, merciful God, and grant, we ask, that we may overcome our own errors, so that we may conquer all our enemies. Through, etc.

[Col. 0083A] Repel from us, Lord, we ask, sacrilegious desires, and grant that we may celebrate the divine (variant: blessed) mysteries with chaste joys. Through, etc.

[Note: In the margin of the codex: “Prayer should be made lest profanation steal upon us.”]

It is truly worthy. We humbly beseech you that all profanation may depart from our hearts, and that what we reject in our profession we may avoid in our actions; for it is utterly detestable that, although you have removed even the adherents of vain superstition, devilish inventions should be handled by your faithful—for it is beyond doubt that the adherents of evil spirits, who are proved by deeds and words to be such, inflict a stain upon morals when crimes are either performed or sung about. We ought all the more readily to rejoice in the newness of heavenly life, once every rite of destructive antiquity has been abolished; for then heavenly pardon will not be lacking, if, having renounced all abominations, we hasten to the saving commands of the true Divinity and sing his praises with holy voice. Through, etc.

[Note: The codex reads corruptly: “Who by this very fact … of the evil spirit, there is no doubt.” We have retained Blanchini’s correction, adopted by Muratori, although another and perhaps better correction may exist.]

May the venerable solemnity of the Sacrament make us joyful, Lord, we ask, and likewise nourish our minds and bodies with spiritual sanctification, and continually exercise us in chaste joys. Through, etc.

Purify your household, Lord, we ask, and cleanse it from every contagion of wickedness. [May they rejoice in your gifts and praise you always and everywhere:] so that the vessels redeemed by the Lord’s Passion may not again be defiled by unclean spirits, but may be possessed by everlasting salvation. Through, etc.

[Note: The words enclosed in brackets seem to have been wrongly inserted into the text. Shortly afterward the codex incorrectly reads *inficiat* (“may defile”), but *salutatio* (“salutation”) is intended.]

### XXXVIII. Another

[Note: A related prayer is found in the Gelasian codex, Book III, no. 61, and in the Roman Missal among the common prayers against persecutors and evildoers.]

Almighty and eternal God, defend us from fear of our enemies, so that, once every disturbance has been removed, we may serve you with free minds. [Col. 0083C] Through, etc.

Grant, we ask, Lord our God, that, even when placed amid every kind of distress, we may not cease to implore your name; and, when heavenly mercy is extended to us, may we never cease from your praise. Through, etc.

May your appeasement be near to us, Lord; although we do not deserve it through our own works, may we receive it through your mercy, anticipated for us by the unique sacrifice. Through, etc.

[Note: A marginal note in the manuscript: “Knock longer, so that the request may be granted.”]

It is truly worthy. For by the example reported in the Gospel you taught us that what we cannot obtain by our merits we may obtain by knocking longer at the door of your mercy. Therefore we humbly ask you to grant us perseverance in prayer and to open the gracious hearing of your propitiation. Through, etc.

[Note: This is read in the codices of Gregory of Muratori on the Twelfth Sunday after Pentecost; in Menardus, on the Thirteenth; in the Roman Missal, on the Eleventh.]

May we experience, Lord, we ask, through receiving your Sacrament, help for mind and body, so that, saved in both, we may glory in the fullness of heavenly healing. Through, etc.

Pour out, we ask, Lord, the Spirit of grace upon your household, and drive out from it whatever of the devil’s deceit has crept in and whatever stain of earthly corruption it has incurred; so that, cleansed within and without, it may always offer you pure devotion and more easily obtain what it reasonably and suitably requests. Through, etc.

### XXXIX. Another

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, recalling the actions of your Sacraments, we may both be relieved by temporal security and instructed by the ordinances of the Law. Through, etc.

[Note: This is found in the codices of Gregory of Muratori on the Fifth Sunday after Pentecost; in Menardus, on the Sixth; in the Roman Missal, on the Fourth.]

Give us, Lord our God, that the course of the world may be directed peacefully for us according to your ordering, and that your Church may rejoice in tranquil devotion. Through, etc.

[Note: It is included in the Roman Missal among the common prayers against persecutors of the Church.]

Protect us, Lord, we ask, as we serve your mysteries, so that we may serve divine things both in body and in mind. Through, etc.

[Note: In the margin of the codex: “The Church of God is exercised by adversity, so that it may be strengthened by prosperity.”]

It is truly worthy. You provide for what will benefit your people and regulate what has been done, and in wondrous ways you govern the helm of your Church, so that she may be exercised by adversity and strengthened by prosperity; lest she either succumb under attack or grow sluggish through security, but, always subject to you in affection, may neither fail to pray in tribulation nor cease to give thanks amid joys. Through, etc.

[Note: The codices of Gregory of Muratori assign this prayer to the Seventh Sunday after Pentecost; Menardus’s codex, to the Eighth; the Roman Missal, to the Sixth.]

We have been filled with your gifts, Lord; grant, we ask, that we may both be cleansed by their effect and fortified by their aid. Through, etc.

[Col. 0084C] May the mercy hoped for come to those who plead, Lord, and may the generosity of heaven be granted to them, so that they may both learn what ought rightly to be asked and receive what they have requested. Through, etc.

### XL. Another

Grant us, Lord, we ask, the help of your grace; without it we can do nothing good, but by its generosity may we be able both worthily to think and to do what belongs to you. Through, etc.

Grant us, Lord our God, that, when we are about to celebrate the solemnities of the saints, we may possess not merely bodily observance but, what is more important, purity of mind. Through, etc.

[Note: A note in the margin of the codex: “Abundance of devotion should be requested.”]
