It is truly worthy. For we trust that your gifts can bestow upon us abundance of devotion and peace, so that rightly practiced religion may grant security, and the security granted may serve the sacred solemnities. (Variant: tranquility.) Through, etc.

[Col. 0085A] Grant us, Lord, we ask, that we may advance both in understanding and in observance of the saving mystery. Through, etc.

Surround your servants, men and women, Lord, with heavenly visitation; pour the dew of your blessing upon their minds and bodies, so that, suitably prepared for the sacred solemnities, they may both bring back the grace of sanctification and obtain what they devoutly pray for. Through, etc.

### XLI. Another

Almighty and eternal God, turn us wholly to yourself in mind, so that you, who grant such gifts to the undeserving, may bestow greater ones upon the devout. Through, etc.

We offer you sacrifices of praise, Lord, who fill us alike with present blessings and with those to come. Through, etc.

[Note: Another marginal note: “Divine protections are always present for harsh and idle workers—that is, for us.”]

It is truly worthy. You lavish immense protections upon idle and harsh workers, and show what great things you can bestow upon those subject to you with their whole heart; and, while you lavish these gifts upon the unworthy, you encourage them to become worthy of receiving better things. Through, etc.

We give you thanks, Lord, who make us breathe again after temporal pressures, so that you may advance us to everlasting joys. Through, etc.

Perfect your mercies toward the people who plead, Lord; by the abundance of your gifts you grant them to ask more earnestly for greater grace and to hope with greater confidence. Through, etc.

### XLII. Another

Look upon the affliction of your people, Lord, we ask, and grant that, once delivered from every need, they may serve you with a tranquil mind. Through, etc.

Make us joyful, Lord, we ask, through your consolations, and, so that you may bestow upon us the gifts of heavenly grace, graciously grant forgiveness. Through, etc.

Form the devotion of our mind, Lord, we ask, so that, together with the offerings of sacrifices, it may present you with a pure heart. Through, etc.

[Note: Also in the margin: “The Lord always cherishes his Church and does not cease to exercise her through his promises.”]

It is truly worthy. You both cherish your Church with benefits and do not cease to exercise her through promises; so that, while granting what is asked, you make what is hoped for be requested with greater confidence, and we ought never to cease offering thanks, even if they are offered continually, since the praises of what has been granted are not silenced and what is still to be granted is rightly entreated. Through, etc.

May the gifts of your Sacrament give us life, Lord, so that through divine participation we may always deserve to increase. Through, etc.

[Col. 0085D] Look graciously upon your servants, men and women, Lord, we ask, so that they may always desire what pleases you and always attain what is salutary for them. Through, etc.

### XLIII. Another

Be present to your people, Lord, and extend the help of your propitiation to those who trust in your mercy. Through, etc.

May the vows of those who plead reach the ears of your mercy, Lord; and, so that we may obtain what we ask, make us always request what pleases you. Through, etc.

Purify us, Lord, by the very Sacraments through which we render our service, so that our offering may likewise be returned to you as sacrifice and action. Through, etc.

[Note: Another marginal note: “The Church of God, when thought to be oppressed, then prevails more powerfully, exalted.”]

It is truly worthy. For you, always perfecting strength in our weakness, have granted that your Church should grow amid adversity, so that, when she was thought to be oppressed, she might then prevail all the more exalted; while affliction both reveals the testing of faith and, overcome by you, makes the present life glorious. Through, etc.

[Note: The codex reads *declinarat* (“had turned aside”). Blanchini thought it should be corrected to *declinat* (“turns aside”). Muratori’s correction seemed preferable.]

Strengthened by the gift of heavenly life, we ask, Lord, that what is a mystery for us in the present life may become a help toward eternity. Through, etc.

Grant your servants, Lord, an abundance of protection and grace. Give health of mind and body. Give continual increases of prosperity, and make them ever devoted to you. Through, etc.

### XLIV. Another

Almighty and eternal God, defend the rulers of the Roman name, so that, trusting in your right hand, they may become stronger than all their enemies. Through, etc.

Grant, we ask, Lord our God, that by the gifts of your grace we, whom you command to offer you the daily sacrifice, may always be justified and instructed. Through, etc.

[Note: In the margin of the codex: “Prosperity is withheld from us so that we may seek heavenly things more swiftly.”]

It is truly worthy. You often withhold the prosperity of present things for this reason: lest, held back by them, we fail to seek heavenly things; and then you bestow those same things more generously, when we are readier to transfer them to the worship of your name. Through, etc.

We offer due praises to your majesty, Lord, who both refresh us with temporal supports and feed us with eternal ones. Through, etc.

[Note: The codex, in a second hand, reads “of eternal peace”; the first hand reads “of eternal peace” with a different inflection, indicating a correction.]

[Note: This prayer, up to “commands,” is found in the codices of Gregory of Muratori and in the Roman Missal on the Thursday after Passion Sunday, where, however, *delectationibus* (“delights”) is read instead of *dilectionibus* (“loves”). This also confirms the reading of our codex, *respuentes et repleantur* (“rejecting … may they be filled”), followed by *gubernati proficiant* (“guided, may they advance”), so that there is no need to correct it to the singular forms *respuens, repleatur, gubernata proficiat*, as Muratori did. For *plebs* (“people”) is a collective noun and may be joined with adjectives and verbs in the plural.]

Be gracious, we ask, to your people, Lord, so that, rejecting from day to day what does not please you, they may rather be filled with love of your commands, and, guided by the consolations of mortal life, may advance toward the fulfillment of immortality. Through, etc.

### XLV. Another

Guard your people, Lord, and, so that you may lavish perpetual mercy upon them, make them ever devoted to your name. Through, etc.

[Col. 0086D] Help your suppliants, Lord, so that those who trust in your goodness may obtain the help of your grace. Through, etc.

God, who graciously bring about the effects of your mysteries, grant, we ask, that our services may become suitable for sacred gifts. Through, etc.

[Note: A marginal note: “All things that impede equity must be rejected.”]

It is truly worthy. You have determined that the human race consists in a just and sincere fellowship; therefore you have taught us to reject everything that hinders equity, because through such things peaceful harmony is disturbed. You command injustice to be avoided so that unanimity may remain unharmed; and we must hasten greatly to reject what does not please you and instead desire what can make you favorable to us. Through, etc.

Having received the support of our salvation, we humbly ask you, Lord, to make worthy those whom you grant to share in so great a mystery. Through, etc.

Be graciously present to your people, Lord, and, so that you may not abandon them in perpetual goodness, exercise them unceasingly in devout works; for you will bestow all the gifts by which you grant an increase of religion. Through, etc.

### XIX. In the month of August

[Note: Thus the codex. Having seen that the Masses following belonged to Saint Stephen the protomartyr, whose Finding is celebrated on the third day before the Nones, Muratori published “the third day before the Nones.” But the title “the fourth day before the Nones of August: the Nativity of Saint Stephen in the cemetery of Callistus on the Appian Way,” agreeing with the Bucherian Catalogue, refers to Pope and Martyr Stephen, buried in the cemetery of Callistus; the Gregorian Sacramentary indeed assigns his Mass to this day. The compiler wrongly placed beneath this title the Masses of Saint Stephen the protomartyr, which, as Mass VII’s preface itself shows, were used after the Nativity of the Lord, as we observed in note 8 in the preface placed before the Sacramentary. More will be said about these Masses of Saint Stephen, especially the prefaces, which display the style and spirit of Leo.]

### IV NONES OF AUGUST. The Nativity of Saint Stephen in the cemetery of Callistus on the Appian Way

#### I

[Note: The Gelasian and Gregorian Sacramentaries assign this prayer to December 26; the Roman Missal, to January 2, the eighth day.]

Almighty and eternal God, who consecrated the first fruits of the martyrs in the blood of the holy Levite Stephen, grant, we ask, that he may exist as an intercessor for us, who prayed even for his persecutors. Through, etc.

We offer sacrifices to your name, Lord, trembling as much at our own merit as we trust in the intercessions of your saints. Grant, we ask, that they may confer upon us both forgiveness and salvation. Through, etc.

[Note: The codex reads *trepidantum* (“of those trembling”). We have adopted Blanchini’s emendation.]

[Col. 0087C] It is truly worthy. For whenever the solemnities of the holy martyrs are recalled, your victories are celebrated and the power of your triumphs is proclaimed, because in them you made both courage for the struggle and the palm of justice flourish. Among them the blessed Levite Stephen shone gloriously. With the Holy Spirit overflowing, not only did the quality of his works show him forth, but the brilliance of his heavenly glory magnified him so greatly that the gaze of his persecutors could not behold it. He appeared so zealous and faithful in ministering that the sacred prerogative of the apostolic tables was entrusted to him. He was so distinguished alike in purity and generosity that he fulfilled the care of widows with mercy and chastity. He was so instructed in divine words that he openly defeated the councils of the Jews; and he was so inflamed by confession of your Son that, after his cross, he was the first to undergo passion. Thus he already penetrated the heavenly kingdoms in mind that, while still established on earth, he saw standing at the right hand of your power the very one for whom he was being stoned; and, forcing heaven, he seized by his merits the crown whose name he bore. Through, etc.

We rejoice, Lord, in the celebration of your saints. Grant, we ask, that those whom we venerate with service we may feel present with their help. Through, etc.

Give your faithful, Lord, we ask, this disposition of love, so that, burning with devotion at the celebration of your saints, they may be entangled in no errors and afflicted by no adversities, but may advance through saving ordinances and be aided by life-giving protections. Through, etc.

#### II. Another

[Note: This prayer is read in Cardinal Thomasius’s Gothic Missal, no. 5.]

Almighty and eternal God, who, adorning the sacred body of your Church with the manifold virtue of your saints, consecrated the first fruits of the martyrs in the blood of the glorious Levite Stephen, grant us to celebrate the day of his Nativity with exceptional honor, since we do not doubt that he specially intercedes for your faithful, he who, imitating the Lord’s charity, prayed even for his persecutors. Through, etc.

Grant us, we ask, Lord our God, that, just as the death of the saints is precious in your sight, so the offering of those who venerate his merits may be acceptable to you. Through, etc.

[Note: The codex incorrectly reads here “may return.” We corrected it from the same prayer repeated below in Mass IV. Muratori conjecturally corrected it to “may return the offering acceptable to you.”]

It is truly worthy. For you not only bestowed upon us through Jesus Christ our Lord, the sons of your adoption, that the sad sting of raging hell and the devil who had received power over it should be trampled underfoot, and that death contracted through sin, while endured for justice, should pass over into reward; but the abundance of your overflowing grace shone forth so greatly that human nature received this not only in the author of our redemption himself but also in the confession of those who believe in him. The holy Stephen, the first Levite and martyr of the New Testament, initiated the beginning of this gift and victory after the Lord’s Passion. Through, etc.

#### III. Another

Graciously grant, Lord, that through this offering we may be cleansed, for which your saints, fighting (variant: confessing) amid torments, attained everlasting glory. Through, etc.

[Note: In Mass V, where this same prayer is repeated with the preface, *dimicantes* (“fighting”) is read instead of *dimicando*, and the variant *confitentes* (“confessing”) is added instead of *confitendo*.]

[Note: The variant reading *sancti* (“holy”) was inserted into the codex. Immediately below, in the preface of Mass V, the reading is *passione sacrasti, cui tantam gratiam* (“you hallowed by [his] passion, upon whom [you bestowed] such great grace”).]

It is truly worthy. For you consecrated this feast of the blessed (variant: holy) Stephen for us as venerable through his passion; the Holy Spirit poured such grace into him that, as the first worker of piety in the Levitical office, he administered the tables; as guardian of widows, he became an example of chastity; renowned for the power of signs, he destroyed the unbelief of the Jews by the power of your word; fervently imploring pardon for those who stoned him in the ardor of charity, he saw the Son of Man standing at the right hand of immense power, with heaven’s secret opened to him; and, before the contest had been completed, he alone openly saw the kingdom of the Lord and Savior, which was shown to all the saints after the struggle.

[Note: In the preface of Mass V: “destroying Jewish unbelief with steadfast voice, imploring Christ’s pardon for those who stoned him as a true follower.”]

[Note: The codex reads “kingdom.” In the preface of Mass V, however, it reads “his reward,” and shortly afterward “is shown.”]

Through, etc.

#### IV. Another

[Note: This prayer is composed partly from the first prayer of Mass I and partly from the first prayer of Mass II.]

Almighty and eternal God, who consecrated the first fruits of the martyrs in the blood of the glorious Levite Stephen, grant us to celebrate the day of his Nativity with exceptional honor, since we do not doubt that he specially intercedes for your faithful, he who, imitating the Lord’s charity, prayed even for his persecutors. Through, etc.

God, author and giver of every gift, who adorn your Church’s sacred body with the manifold virtue of the saints, grant that she may be defended by the prayer of those members in whose excellence she glories. Through, etc.

[Note: Here the second prayer of Mass II is brought in again.]

Grant us, we ask, Lord our God, that, just as in your sight, etc.

It is truly worthy. For you not only bestowed upon us through Jesus Christ our Lord that the sad sting of evident hell and the devil who had received power over it should be trampled underfoot; but also that this should be received in the confession of those who believe in the same Son of yours, etc.

[Note: The preface of Mass II follows.]

#### V. Another

[Note: See above, the first prayer of Mass III.]

Graciously grant, Lord, we ask, that through this offering, etc.

It is truly worthy. For you consecrated for us this feast, etc.

[Note: The preface of Mass III is resumed; its variants were given there.]

#### VI. Another

God, author and giver of the gifts to be offered to you, grant that the sacrifice which bestowed glory upon the holy martyrs in persecution may become for us a protection in devotion. Through, etc.

[Note: The word “sacrifice” has been added from a similar prayer of Mass I for the Nativity of Saint Xystus.]

It is truly worthy. On this day of solemnity, on which Saint Stephen, the first candidate of your faith, was stoned by the persecution of unbelievers so that he might exist as the living stone of sacred confession and fulfill what he bore under his distinguished name through the crown of martyrdom. Through, etc.

Almighty and eternal God, who grant those established in earthly substance to handle divine things, grant, through the prayers of your saints, that we may attain the same by a heavenly manner of life. Through, etc.

Preserve, we ask, Lord, the service of your children subject to you, so that, through the intercession of the saints, they may be worthy of your redemption and always be filled with your grace. Through, etc.

#### VII. Another

[Note: This is found in the Gregorian Sacramentaries on December 26.]

God, who mercifully redeemed us through the incarnation of your Only-Begotten, grant us the continual protection of your saints, by which we may be able to receive a portion of the saving mystery. Through, etc.

[Note: It is read in the Gelasian Sacramentary, Book I, no. 6.]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the blessed Stephen, the glorious Levite, just as he shone before others as an imitator of the Lord’s passion and compassion, may likewise be a ready helper of our weakness. Through, etc.

We come before you, Lord, amid the wondrous benefits of our redemption and the glorious solemnities of the holy martyrs, with gifts, giving thanks both for the abundance of healing and for the provision of intercession. Through, etc.

[Note: This preface is found in the codices of Gregory of Pamelia and Menardus, and also at the end of the Ottobonian manuscript in Muratori, volume II, page 292.]

It is truly worthy. Recalling the Nativity of the Levite and martyr Saint Stephen, who set before us venerable examples of faith, sacred service, administration, outstanding chastity, marvelous preaching, steadfastness, confession, and patience; therefore he rightly follows the Nativity of your Son with the solemnity of his passion before all others, since the first martyr went forth to meet his everlasting glory. Through, etc.

#### VIII. Another

We humbly sacrifice offerings to you, Lord, proclaiming the saving supports bestowed upon us in the holy martyrs. Through, etc.

It is truly worthy. For you are wondrous in your saints; and although in each of them we ought to render the fitting service that pertains to the worship of Divinity, nevertheless we unquestionably proclaim you in all of them, since every wonder declares you in the triumphs of the blessed martyrs. [Col. 0090C] Through, etc.

[Note: It is included in the Gelasian Sacramentary, Book I, no. 6, and in the codices of Gregory of Pamelia and Menardus.]

We give you thanks, Lord, for your mercies multiplied toward us: you save us through the birth of your Son and sustain us through the prayers of the blessed martyrs. Through, etc.

God, founder and restorer of the human race, grant, we ask, that your people, instructed by saving Sacraments and supported by protections, may receive present gifts in such a way that they may deserve to attain eternal ones. Through, etc.

#### IX. Another

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, just as throughout all the regions of the world you cause the victories of your martyrs to spread, so, with you helping us, we may everywhere experience their presence. Through, etc.

[Note: This is found in the same Gelasian Sacramentary, no. 6, and in Gregory’s Sacramentary apud Pamelium.]

May the gifts of today’s devotion, which the glorious commemoration of your blessed martyr Stephen brings forth, be pleasing to you, Lord, we ask. Through, etc.

It is truly worthy. Rejoicing on this feast, on which the blessed martyr Stephen marked with his own honor the basilica dedicated to your name, we honor the venerable Levite: an example of chastity, a faithful dispenser of apostolic nourishment under the New Testament, a ready defender amid opponents, and the first consecrator of heavenly martyrdom. Through, etc.

[Note: The ancient basilica of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill seems to be indicated; the *Pontifical Book* says that Pope Simplicius dedicated it. The codex corruptly reads “the basilica dedicated to your name.”]

Filled, Lord, both with your Sacraments and with the joys of the desired celebration, we ask that the prayers of those whose commemorations are being offered here may bring us healing. Through, etc.

[Note: It is read in Menardus’s Gregorian Sacramentary and in the Roman Missal on September 27, the Nativity of Saints Cosmas and Damian.]

Protect your people, Lord, we ask, both the participation in the heavenly banquet that has been granted and the intercession bestowed by the righteous. Through, etc.

## XX. The Eighth Day before the Ides of August

[Note: In the Bucherian Catalogue: “The eighth day before the Ides of August: Pope Xystus at Callistus and Praetextatus—corrected from our Sacramentary to ‘and at Praetextatus’—Agapitus and Felicissimus.”]

### The Nativity of Saint Xystus in the cemetery of Callistus; and of Felicissimus and Agapitus in the cemetery of Praetextatus on the Appian Way

#### I

God, the strength of all the saints, who bestowed upon them the abundant gift of grace by which they came to this glory, grant, we ask, forgiveness of our sins, so that we may be able to celebrate their solemnities worthily. Through, etc.

Author and giver of the gifts to be offered to you, grant that this unique sacrifice, which bestowed glory upon your saints in passion, may grant us protection in devotion. Through, etc.

It is truly worthy. For among the countless palms of martyrs with which the circuit of this city has been especially crowned, you also consecrated this venerable day for us by the blood of your blessed priest and martyr Xystus. Through, etc.

#### II. Another

Almighty and eternal God, who granted your saints not only to believe in your Son but also to suffer for him, extend divine help to our weakness as well, so that we may deserve, at least by sincere confession, the everlasting mercy for which they breathed out their blessed souls. Through, etc.

You magnified your saints, Lord, when they accepted suffering for Christ. Grant, we ask, that what we have humbly celebrated may also purify us. Through, etc.

It is truly worthy. Recalling with due solemnity the natal day of your holy martyr and priest Xystus, who, a worthy successor of the apostolic pontificate in his age and a most courageous imitator in passion, received the persecutor’s sword upon his fearless neck, rejoicing to be beheaded for him from whom he could not be severed. Through, etc.

#### III. Another

Grant, we ask, Lord, that your saints may continually pray for us and always be mercifully heard. Through, etc.

May your holy gifts benefit us unto salvation, through the intercession of those who pleased you, Lord; and may the guilt of mortality not render unworthy those whom your redemption makes innocent. Through, etc.

[Note: It is found in the Gregorian Sacramentary apud Menardus and among the prefaces of the Ottobonian manuscript of Gregory apud Muratori, volume II, page 328.]

It is truly worthy. On this day of celebration, when the blessed Xystus, priest and martyr alike, joyfully poured out devoted blood to you, he encouraged the children of his teaching to earn the same glory, and those whom he instructed by exhortation he preceded by example. Through, etc.

Have mercy and grant us an increase of your faith, Lord, so that the faith that glorifies your holy martyrs because they held it to the shedding of blood may also justify us as we truly follow it. Through, etc.

[Note: This is another Mass with another preface, although the compiler did not assign it a separate number.]

May the intercessions pleasing to you of the saints be present with us, Lord, and may their prayer commend what we bring for their solemnity. Through, etc.

It is truly worthy. You granted your holy martyr Xystus, the chief priest, not only the triumph of his own passion but also that he might benefit the ministers of the Church subject to him. In the end, the glorious man was followed neither by inferior blessedness nor by a slower victory than that of his disciple. Through, etc.

#### IV. Another

Be present to our supplications, Lord, and, through the intercession of your saints, graciously defend us from the attacks of our enemies. Through, etc.

Receive, Lord, the gifts dedicated to the passions of your saints, and may those gifts which supplied them with strength amid persecutions provide us with steadfastness amid adversities. Through, etc.

It is truly worthy. On this day you crowned the holy Xystus, priest of the apostolic see, with a blessed martyrdom. Rejoicing in these works and gifts of yours with manifold thanksgiving, we offer you sacrifices of praise. Through, etc.

Continued correction is indeed beneficial to sinners, Lord. But, we ask, let it be tempered through the intercession of your saints, so that we, though weak, may not fail, but may be able through your grace to amend ourselves when corrected. Through, etc.

Defend, we ask, Lord, your people, who trust in the forgiveness of your mercy alone; and, through the intercession of your saints, may whatever is owed to them for the correction of sin pass over into the effect of consolation. Through, etc.

#### V. Another

Be present through the prayer of the holy martyrs, Lord, and make those who were granted to suffer for your name intercede for your faithful. Through, etc.

Lord our God, purify us through your Sacraments, and grant that those whom you allow to participate in their mysteries may rejoice in everlasting remedies. Through, etc.

It is truly worthy. For a festive solemnity is celebrated for you, a consecrated day is observed for you, on which, anticipating the Nativity of the holy Xystus, the apostolic bishop, whose venerable blood was poured out in confession of your name, we pay annual vows to your majesty. Through, etc.

[Col. 0093A] [Note: The Gregorian codices present this collect on August 24, at the feast of Saint Eusebius the priest; the Roman Missal does so on the same day and elsewhere more than once.]

Refreshed by heavenly food and drink, our God, we humbly beseech you that, in whose commemoration we have received these gifts, we may be fortified by their prayers as well. Through, etc.

Extend your mercy, Lord, and be the defender and guardian of your people, so that they may be able to attend the venerable solemnities of your saints in secure assembly. Through, etc.

#### VI. Another

[Note: The same Missal assigns this prayer to June 9, at the feast of the holy martyrs Primus and Felician.]

Grant, we ask, Lord, that we may always follow the feasts of your saints, through whose intercession we may experience the gifts of your protection. Through, etc.

Grant, we ask, Lord our God, that we may always live through your Sacraments, for you do not cease to protect those whom you have permitted always to cling to your mysteries. Through, etc.

[Note: Thus the codex. “You will not cease,” which Muratori adopted, would be more pleasing.]

It is truly worthy. For the desired feast of your holy priest and martyr Xystus is present for us; venerating it in its annual return, we offer you sacrifices of praise with the angels, etc.

We have been filled with your mercy, Lord, and with the blessing of the saints, and have been relieved by the gift of security. Through, etc.

#### VII. Another

God, who have granted us to reach with joy the Nativity of your holy bishop and martyr Xystus, grant, we ask, that, just as we celebrate it with secure minds, so we may celebrate it with worthy observances. Through, etc.

Receive, Lord, the gifts we bring to you at their solemnity, whose intercessions we know deliver us. Through, etc.

It is truly worthy. For we recognize the effects of your goodness, Lord, by which you did not wish us to omit even amid the world’s former tribulations the solemnities—always to be honored—of your glorious priest and martyr Xystus; and now, with freedom restored, you grant that we may venerate them. Through, etc.

[Note: The codex incorrectly reads *ideo* (“therefore”).]

### At the Nativity of Saints Felicissimus and Agapitus

Magnifying your clemency, Lord, we humbly beseech you: since you make us take part in the frequent nativities of your saints, grant us to rejoice in everlasting fellowship with them. Through, etc.

Grant us, almighty God, always to praise you in the commemoration of your saints, because you will take care to sustain those whom you have permitted to persevere in your honor. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0093D] In the Gregorian manuscripts and in the Roman Missal it is read on the 22nd, at the feast of Saints Timothy, Hippolytus, and Symphorianus, and elsewhere.]

May the offering of the consecrated people, made for the honor of your saints, be acceptable to you, Lord; for it recognizes that through their merits it has received help amid tribulation. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For you have always caused us joyfully to celebrate the ever-desired feasts of Saints Felicissimus and Agapitus, and you who granted steadfast faith amid adversity will restore the benefits (another reading: gifts) of freedom. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0094D] It appears in the Roman Missal on August 1, in the commemoration of the Maccabees.]

Grant, Lord, we ask, that as we recall their memory by participation in the sacrament, so also, by advancing in faith, we may follow them. Through, etc.

Look upon your family subject to you, Lord, and more earnestly regard its thanksgiving, since you deigned to hear its prayers in sorrow. Through, etc.

## XXI. The Fourth Ides of August. The Feast of Saint Lawrence

### I

God, who preserve us by the protection of the holy martyrs, grant that your Church may worthily celebrate the solemnities of such men [Col. 0094B] and that they may continually plead with you for us. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0094D] This is the Mass of the vigil under the same title, together with the other prayers of the feast day.]

Truly it is worthy. We anticipate the feast day of blessed Lawrence, who was venerable both as a levite and as a martyr, gloriously distinguished by his particular office, and exalted by a memorable and resplendent passion. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0094D] In the Gregorian codices this occurs on August 11, in the Mass of Saint Tiburtius. The Roman Missal has the same prayer, with slight variation, on that day and on the feast of Saint Bartholomew.]

We have received, Lord, the pledge of eternal redemption. Through the intervention of your saints, grant, we ask, that it may be for us both a help in the present life and likewise in the life to come. Through, etc.

Be present, Lord, to your people, and make him whom you grant to attend the gatherings of your saints secure through perpetual protection. Through, etc.

### II. Another

Grant us, Lord, your manifold grace in the celebration of blessed Lawrence the martyr, [Col. 0094C] so that the Christian people may learn from so great a contest both to be strengthened by firm patience and to rejoice in holy victory. Through, etc.

For the venerable passion of blessed Lawrence the martyr, we humbly sacrifice to you, Lord, offerings which will be pleasing through the prayer of the one for whose merits they are offered. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. We earnestly beseech your majesty, who granted us this day to venerate the martyrdom of Saint Lawrence, whom you had so imbued with every kind of piety that he himself was both altar and sacrifice, both priest and temple. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0094D] The Gregorian codices and the Roman Missal have this collect on August 18 and elsewhere.]

You have satisfied your family with sacred gifts, Lord. Through the intercession of the one whose solemnities we celebrate, refresh us always, we ask. Through, etc.

[Col. 0094D] Almighty and everlasting God, look favorably upon the petitions of your Church, so that she may be helped by the merits of blessed Lawrence the martyr, in whose passion she rejoices. Through, etc.

### III. Another

You have magnified your saints [Col. 0095A] by their passion suffered for Christ. Grant, we ask, that, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0095D] The same prayer is found in the second Mass of Saint Xystus, on the eighth day before the Ides of August.]

Truly it is worthy. For you are the unconquerable strength of all the saints, and amid the adversities of worldly life you console us by the outstanding glorification of the blessed martyrs; through the triumph of Saint Lawrence, whom we celebrate today, you kindle us toward the sublime examples of endurance. Through, etc.

Filled, Lord, with your gifts on the feast of your saints, grant that we may experience as aids these holy mysteries which we celebrate with our prayers. Through, etc.

### IV. Another

[Note: [Col. 0095D] A related prayer appears in the Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal on December 26, the feast of Saint Stephen.]

Receive, we ask, Lord, the gifts joyfully offered for the commemoration of your saints, and may that which made them glorious through suffering make us innocent through devotion. Through, etc.

[Col. 0095B] Truly it is worthy. For by your gifts and offerings we venerate today the passion of blessed Lawrence the martyr. In confessing Jesus Christ, your Son, he received with ardent spirit various punishments; he overcame the fires laid beneath him and the changing tortures devised by the cruel ingenuity of his persecutors with unwavering strength; and though his limbs were consumed, he remained victorious in mind, firm in his inner being. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0095D] It is found in all the Gregorian manuscripts on Saint Lawrence’s day, but in the Roman Missal on the day of his octave.]

Stir up your Spirit in your Church, Lord, whom Saint Lawrence the levite served, so that, filled by that same Spirit, we may strive to love what he loved and to practice by our deeds what he taught. Through, etc.

### V. Another

May the offering of our service be acceptable to you, Lord, and, through the prayers of blessed Lawrence, for whose commemoration it is presented, may it prove salutary for us. [Col. 0095C] Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. By this act of devotion, for the solemnity of Saint Lawrence the martyr, we offer you a sacrifice of praise, because through the working of your power it came about that no accusations of the impious, no ferocity of persecutors, and no cruelty of dreadful punishments could overcome the man set aflame by your Spirit. Through, etc.

### VI. Another

[Note: [Col. 0095D] You will find this prayer in the Roman Missal on October 9, at the feast of Saints Dionysius and his companions. Then, in the codex, *pro nos* is incorrectly written *nobis*.]

Graciously receive, we ask, Lord, the gifts offered to you by your people for the honor of your saints, and sanctify us through their intercession. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. Recalling the annual vows of blessed Lawrence, who was an outstanding steward and an exceptional confessor of your name, even unto bloodshed, the blessed martyr offered an example of ecclesiastical piety and of bearing witness to your Son, our Lord, especially in caring for the poor. [Col. 0095D] Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0096D] In the Gelasian Sacramentary, the Gregorian Sacramentary, and the Roman Missal it is the first prayer of the Mass of Saint Lawrence’s vigil.]

Be present to our supplications, Lord, and through the intercession of Saint Lawrence, your martyr, graciously bestow upon us perpetual mercy. Through, etc.

### VII. Another

[Note: [Col. 0096D] It is found in the Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal on Saint Lawrence’s day.]

Receive, we ask, Lord, the gifts worthily offered, and grant, through the supporting merits of blessed Lawrence, that they may become a help toward our salvation. [Col. 0096D] Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For the honor of blessed Lawrence, your martyr, we offer you sacrifices of praise. Through, etc.

Refreshed by the taste of your grace and strengthened by the sweetness of the heavenly table, we give you thanks. Through, etc.

Hear, we ask, Lord, the prayers of your family, and grant us through the intercession of your saints what we do not deserve through our own actions. Through, etc.

### VIII. Another

With the supplications of your saints, Lord, we implore you to make the service of our ministry pleasing to you as we offer these sacred gifts. Through, etc.

[Col. 0096B] Truly it is worthy. For whatever we undertake through the merits of your saints returns to your praise and glory, you who are always wonderful in their strength. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0096D] It is found in Book II, no. 43, of the Gelasian Sacramentary, at Vespers, and in the Gregorian books of Menardus and Pamelius.]

May the just prayer of Saint Lawrence protect us, Lord, and may what our conscience does not presume to ask be granted us through the prayer of him who pleased you. Through, etc.

### IX. Another

We humbly ask you, God, that through the intervention of blessed Lawrence the martyr you may multiply your gifts in us and order our times. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0096D] A related prayer is the prayer of the Mass of Saint Thomas the Apostle in the Roman Missal.]

We render the due service of our devotion, humbly asking that you guard your gifts in us through his intercession, for whose honored confession we offer you a sacrifice of praise. Through, etc.

[Col. 0096C] Truly it is worthy. We ask from your mercy that, as we celebrate the merits of those in honor of your name, so we may strive to imitate their holy works. Through, etc.

Protect us, Lord, by the prayers of Saint Lawrence, your martyr, so that we may always deserve to increase in grace, since we place our confidence in the protection of such patrons. Through, etc.

### X. Another

May the feast of Saint Lawrence, your martyr, always receive us joyfully, Lord, we ask; may it pour into us the gladness of his glorification and make us acceptable to you. Through, etc.

Complete for us, Lord, the fruit of today’s thanksgiving, so that through the prayers of blessed Lawrence the martyr, this offering—anticipating in devotion his feast day—may be fulfilled in perfect joy. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. We implore your mercy: grant that you may continually bestow upon our minds the sweetness of Saint Lawrence, your martyr, so that we may love the merit of his passion and that he, our ever-faithful patron, may always obtain pardon for us. Through, etc.

We give you thanks, Lord, because, through your inspiration, we love Saint Lawrence, your martyr, so that, as we anticipate his feast day, [Col. 0097A] we may always be cherished by his devout intercessions and merits. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0097D] The word *praeeuntes* indicates that this Mass concerns the vigil.]

### XI. Another

Increase, we ask, Lord, the faith of your people, conceived from the feast of Saint Lawrence the martyr, so that we may not be frightened by any adversity from hastening to confess your name, but rather may be urged on by the contemplation of such great virtue. Through, etc.

May the patronage of the saints pleasing to you be with us, Lord, so that what we bring for their solemnity may be commended by their prayer. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0097D] It is found in Book II, no. 43, of the Gelasian Sacramentary.]

Truly it is worthy. On this day of solemnity, when you received the acceptable offering of blessed Lawrence through the glorious contest of his chaste body, the living limbs placed upon the coals crackled; yet it was not the punishment of one suffering, but the incense of devout confession. Nor did the martyr wish to be freed from earthly torment, but he prayed to be crowned in heaven. [Col. 0097B] Through, etc.

### XII. Another

Hear, we ask, Lord, our prayers, so that we may receive with favorable result the solemnities of Saint Lawrence, your martyr, which we anticipate by the worship due to you. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0097D] This prayer belongs to the vigil of Saint Lawrence. In the Gelasian codex it is placed in the vigil of all the apostles, Book II, no. 34.]

We precede the feast of Saint Lawrence, your martyr, with our gifts, Lord, so that what is hindered by the obstacle of our conscience may be made acceptable through his merits. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. Although the glory of your saints, propagated by you, Lord, is renowned throughout the whole world [Note: [Col. 0097D] Thus the codex. In Muratori, *data*.], nevertheless Rome rejoices especially in the solemnity of blessed Lawrence; for, born a citizen, [Col. 0097C] a sacred minister, [Note: [Col. 0097D] These words are very disordered and can be repaired only with difficulty. Muratori, conjecturally following Blanchinius, printed *dedicatum* instead of *et dicatum*.] and a gift dedicated to your name, he is peculiarly hers. Through your grace, he was an outstanding executor of the stewardship entrusted to him; he merited martyrdom as his reward and attained the passion through which he became a heavenly being. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0097D] Let those who deny that Saint Lawrence was Roman take note of this.]

May the intercession of blessed Lawrence, your martyr, Lord, merit for us the fullness of joys arising from his confession. Through, etc.

May your people rejoice, Lord, we ask, in the commemoration of Saint Lawrence; and may the one whose devoted service brings them joy raise them up through the desired intercession. Through, etc.

### XIII. Another

[Note: [Col. 0097D] It is found in the Gelasian Sacramentary, Book II, no. 43, and in the Gregorian book of Menardus.]

May the blessing of Saint Lawrence the martyr be with us in the glorification of you, Lord; today his confession has become our intercession through your power. Through, etc.

[Col. 0098A] We offer sacrifices, Lord, rejoicing in the feast (another reading: confession) of Saint Lawrence, your martyr; through your working, Lord, it has brought us both help and advancement. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. With rejoicing hearts we celebrate the precious death of Saint Lawrence, your martyr, which we see, because you conquer, to have conquered the devil. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0097D] In the Gelasian Sacramentary, with a few changes, it is adapted to the vigil of Saint Lawrence, no. 42. In Muratori’s Gregorian codices it is adapted to the Mass of a single confessor; in the Roman Missal, to the common Mass of a confessor-bishop, as well as to the vigil of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle and other feasts.]

Grant us, almighty God, that the venerable solemnity of blessed Lawrence, your martyr, may increase both our devotion and our salvation. Through, etc.

## For the octave

### XIV. Another

Accompany us, Lord, with the continual solemnity of your saints, so that we who are hindered by our own merits may be helped by the prayers of those who pleased you. Through, etc.

[Col. 0098B] May the prayer of Saint Lawrence, your martyr, commend us, Lord, so that, being favorable, you may regard our sacrifices. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For you are always glorious in the strength of your saints. And whenever we recall their feasts, we confess you to be marvelous. Through, etc.

May the repeated solemnity of Saint Lawrence protect us, Lord, and may his blessed intercession win for us your mercy. Through, etc.

## The Ides of August. The Feast of Saints Hippolytus and Pontianus

[Note: [Col. 0098D] In the Bucherian Calendar: “On the Ides of August: Hippolytus at the Tiburtine cemetery and Pontianus at the cemetery of Callistus.” It seems that two different cemeteries required distinct Masses: one for Saint Hippolytus, celebrated at the cemetery on the Tiburtine Way, and another for Saint Pontianus, at the cemetery of Callistus. The following common Mass is adapted to Saint Hippolytus; hence it is also read adapted to the Masses of other saints, with their names inserted.]

### I

God, who preserve us through the multitude of holy martyrs, grant that we may be continually helped by unceasing assistance from those whose solemnities we frequent. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0098D] This prayer is the secret prayer in the Mass of Saint Hippolytus both in the Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal.]

Look favorably, Lord, upon the gifts of your people at this votive feast of the saints, and may the testimony of your truth advance us toward salvation. [Col. 0098C] Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0098D] See above, the preface of the fifth Mass of Saint Xystus.]

Truly it is worthy. For this festive solemnity is celebrated for you, Lord; this consecrated day is observed for you. The blood of Saint Hippolytus, your martyr, poured out in testimony to your truth, marked it with the magnificent honor of your name. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0098D] It is read in Gregorian manuscripts and in the Roman Missal on June 2, at the feast of Saints Marcellinus and Peter, and at other feasts.]

Satisfied with the sacred gift, we humbly beseech you, Lord, that what we celebrate by the service of our due devotion we may experience as an increase of your salvation. Through, etc.

God, who both glorify and protect your Church through the countless patronage of the saints, grant that she may experience the intercession of those whose assembly she celebrates. Through, etc.

### II. Another

Protect us, Lord, by the perpetual protection of the saints, and the more fragile we are, the more raise us up by the help we need. [Col. 0099A] Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0099D] You have this prayer after communion in the Mass of Saints Primus and Felicianus on June 2, in Menardus and in the Roman Missal.]

We ask, almighty God, that the solemnity celebrated through the heavenly mysteries of your saints may obtain for us the forgiveness of your favor. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. You not only repay our evils with good, but, in order to grant more abundant gifts to the miserable, you have provided those who can worthily intercede for us; and what our conscience did not possess is supplied by the intercession of the just, pleasing to you. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0099D] This appears to be a new Mass, which should have been entitled “The Fifteenth Day before the Kalends of September. The Feast of Saint Agapitus.” On that day this feast, with its Mass, is recorded in Book II, no. 48, of the Gelasian Sacramentary and in the Gregorian codices. Others wrongly prefer to suppose that the name Agapitus was written in error for Hippolytus. But the confusion of two Masses into one sometimes occurs in our compiler.]

May the venerable feast of the holy martyr Agapitus, Lord, bring us an increase of saving help. Through, etc.

May your people always rejoice, Lord, in the honor of your saints, and may they receive through their intercession the votive assistance [Col. 0099B] in whose patronage they rejoice. Through, etc.

## XXIII. The Third Day before the Kalends of September. The Feast of Saints Adauctus and Felix

### I

Grant us, almighty God, that we may always follow the feasts of those whose worthy intervention for us we trust in. Through, etc.

As we recall the feast days of Saints Felix and Adauctus, we offer a gift which, through their intercession, Lord, we ask may be pleasing to you. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. With rejoicing we recall the glory of the holy martyrs, in whom we recognize the wondrous effects of your majesty and the patronage prepared for us. [Col. 0099C] Through, etc.

We give you thanks, Lord, because you refresh us both through participation in the heavenly sacrament and through the celebration of your righteous saints. Through, etc.

### II. Another

[Note: [Col. 0100D] Thus the Gregorian codices and the Roman Missal at the feast of these same martyrs on August 30.]

We humbly beseech your majesty, Lord, that just as you continually gladden us by the commemoration of your saints, so you may always defend us through their supplication. Through, etc.

May our sacrifices be as pleasing, we ask, Lord, as the merits of your holy martyrs, for whose solemnities they are presented, are pleasing to you. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. Although we always rejoice in the celebration of your mystery, we rejoice more abundantly through its gift when it is offered for the solemnity of the holy martyrs, through whom we are commended to you. [Col. 0099D] Through, etc.

Satisfied with heavenly gifts as we recall your saints, we give you thanks. Through, etc.

[Col. 0100A] For your family, Lord, we ask that the venerable prayer of the holy martyrs intercede, so that the family which does not abandon their solemnities with devoted mind, aided by their holy protection, may receive both consolation and salvation. Through, etc.

### III. Another

We ask you, Lord our God, that your saints may not cease to pray for our sins, since you willed to be entreated by them on behalf of sinners. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0100D] It appears in the Roman Missal among the common Masses of a single confessor who is not a bishop.]

Grant us, we ask, almighty God, that the offering of our humility may be pleasing both for the honor of your saints and may purify us alike in body and mind. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. We pray for your power, lest the nations say, “Where is their God?” Rather, graciously show that our sins have no greater power to destroy us than either the abundant patronage of the righteous or the unconquerable mercy of your majesty has to save us. [Col. 0100B] Through, etc.

We humbly ask you, God, that we be neither weighed down by our own evils nor attacked by enemies, since we are strengthened by such great merits of your saints. Through, etc.

### IV. Another

We ask, Lord, that you defend us by the protection of your saints, whose continual feasts you use to console us. Through, etc.

May your people always rejoice, Lord, in the saving sacrifice, through which due honor is offered to the holy martyrs and the gift of your sanctification is obtained. Through, etc.

[Col. 0100C] Truly it is worthy. We glorify you in the honor of your saints, for you have granted them everlasting blessedness and prepared such intercessions for our weakness that you can hear them on our behalf. Through, etc.

Hear our prayers, Lord, we ask, so that your people, established under such great patronage, may be freed from their offenses and protected from every adversity. Through, etc.

### V. Another

[Note: [Col. 0100D] This prayer is frequently used in Muratori’s Gregorian manuscripts on August 8, at the feast of Saints Cyriacus and his companions; on April 28, at the feast of Saint Vitalis; and elsewhere. In the Roman Missal it appears among the common Masses of a martyr who is not a bishop.]

May our devotion be acceptable in your sight, Lord, so that, through the supplication of those for whose solemnity it is offered, it may become salutary for us. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. Today the Church frequents its own sacrifice and, in an annual celebration, celebrates anew the feast of the gift once sacrificed—the gift by which, for the confession or name of the one who redeemed her with his blood, she presented the service of her own blood. [Col. 0100D] Through, etc.

### VI. Another

[Note: [Col. 0100D] It is found in the Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal on the feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian; in the same Missal it is also adapted to the feast of the Holy Innocents and to other solemnities.]

May the devout prayer of your saints never be absent for us, Lord, [Note: [Col. 0099D] [ [Col. 0099D] This note appears at the foot of column 99, but the callout letter (c) has not been printed in the text.] On this day the Mass of Saints Adauctus and Felix is read in Gregorian manuscripts [Col. 0100D]. Only the first Mass has a proper prayer.] [Col. 0101A] a prayer that both commends our gifts and always obtains your forgiveness for us. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. For your eternal providence bestowed upon your Church, destined to be propagated throughout the whole world, not only the passion of your Only-Begotten, but also, for the conferral of greater glory, granted that your saints should offer their mutual deaths to you with precious devotion. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0101D] The Roman Missal presents this prayer at the feast of the Holy Innocents and elsewhere.]

We have received votive gifts, Lord; through the prayers of the saints, grant, we ask, that they may bring us protection both for the present life and for the eternal one. Through, etc.

### VII. Another

Be present to your people, Lord, and grant your mercy to those who supplicate you with the patronage of your saints, so that, because they trust in your governance, they may not be overcome by any adversities. Through, etc.

[Col. 0101B] [Note: [Col. 0101D] This preface belongs to the apostles.]

Truly it is worthy. For, as the sacred word declares, precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints. It cannot in any way be explained by what means this glorious death is accounted worthy. They die rejected, and they gain dominion over the world. They die ignorant of worldly learning, and they emerge as teachers of heavenly doctrine. They die as fish-catchers, and become fishers of human beings. They die accustomed to exploring the seas in the ordinary practice of their craft, and are made examiners and judges of the age. And therefore, with the angels, etc.

## XXIV. In the Month of September. The Seventeenth Day before the Kalends of October. The Feast of Saints Cornelius and Cyprian

[Note: [Col. 0101D] In the Bucherian Calendar this day is recorded as follows: “On the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October, Cyprian of Africa; at Rome, celebrated at Callistus.” The name of Cornelius has dropped out, although both our Sacramentary and the Gelasian and Gregorian Sacramentaries place it together with Cyprian on this same day. The ancienter veneration of these martyrs is also indicated by the Canon of the Mass, where the names of Cornelius and Cyprian are read.]

[Col. 0101C] Almighty and everlasting God, who gladden us by the manifold feast of your saints, grant that we may be protected by the patronage of those whose commemoration brings us joy. Through, etc.

Look favorably, Lord, upon the offerings of your people, through which we celebrate, in honor of your name, the passion of the holy martyrs and humbly implore forgiveness for ourselves. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0101D] The prayers marked H—that is, prayers to be included and written below—should have been placed below in the Mass of Saint Euphemia, to which the entire context belongs. They have therefore been inserted here outside their proper place.]

### Prayers H at Saint Euphemia

Truly it is worthy. For your works are immense and truly great (another reading: wondrous). You granted that the human being, once struck down by the devil’s deceit, should through Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, become the victor over his conqueror; [Note: [Col. 0101D] Father Blanchinius judges that this passage should be restored as follows: “the victor, so that this same adversary of his might be subdued not only by the male sex of your faithful,” etc.] and you caused this same adversary [Col. 0102A] not only to be subdued thereafter by the male sex of your faithful, but also to be overcome by feminine weakness, so that she who is more fragile in her condition might be made stronger than the enemy of spiritual substance. Avenging the deception of Eve our mother, she triumphed over the enemy of the human race, who through her had found an entrance for death. These reversals, belonging to your ineffable glory, we venerate in the passion of the holy martyr Euphemia [Note: [Col. 0102D] “We venerate” would be preferable.]. Through, etc.

Receive, Lord, we ask, the services of our devotion, so that, with the saints interceding, what we offer for the honor of your majesty may grant us everlasting life. Through, etc.

Having received the heavenly sacraments, Lord, we give thanks to your gracious name, for you both accompany us with the continual feast of your saints and never cease to give us life through your divine gift. [Col. 0102B] Through, etc.

Look favorably, Lord, upon the service owed to you by your people, so that amid the uncertainties of human weakness they may not be overcome by any adversity, since they trust in your protection. Through, etc.

### Another

[Note: [Col. 0102D] In Book II, no. 57, of the Gelasian Sacramentary, the first three prayers of this Mass are found. In Menardus’s Gregorian codex, only the first two, together with the preface, occur on this same feast day; the first is in the Roman Missal.]

May the feasts of the blessed martyrs and likewise bishops Cornelius and Cyprian protect us, Lord, we ask, and may their venerable prayer commend and gladden us. Through, etc.

Look favorably, Lord, upon the gifts of your people, which are dedicated to your majesty for the solemnities of the holy martyrs Cornelius and Cyprian. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0102D] This preface is read in Muratori’s Gregorian codices, volume II, page 335.]

Truly it is worthy. To proclaim your power in the holy martyrs Cornelius and likewise Cyprian: feeding sacred flocks with divine bread in regions separated from one another, you crowned them in one faith and on the same day—though at different times—with harmonious and equal confession of your name. [Col. 0102C] Through, etc.

Strengthened by the sacred gift, may the prayer of the holy martyrs Cornelius and Cyprian commend us to you, Lord, as we celebrate their feast days. [Col. 0102C] Through, etc.

Extend the right hand of your majesty, Lord, for the defense of the faithful; and so that they may be fortified by the perpetual protection of your mercy, may the continual intercession of the holy martyrs not be lacking for them. Through, etc.

## XXV. The Sixteenth Day before the Kalends of October. The Feast of Saint Euphemia

[Note: [Col. 0102D] Saint Euphemia is not mentioned in the Bucherian Calendar. Nevertheless, on this day the Mass of this holy martyr is recorded in the Gregorian Sacramentaries, while in the Gelasian it is listed on the Ides of April. Perhaps the cult of this martyr, famous at Chalcedon after the Council of Chalcedon, at which Saint Euphemia’s name is praised in many places, was introduced into the Roman Church while Saint Leo was still alive. The following prefaces are not unworthy of his genius.]

### I

[Note: [Col. 0102D] It is in the Roman Missal on July 12, at the feast of Saints Nabor and Felix.]

Grant, Lord, we ask, that just as the feast days of your saints do not cease to be celebrated, so their intercessions may continually accompany us. [Col. 0103A] Through, etc.

With gratitude we hasten together to dedicate gifts, which, Lord, we humbly sacrifice to your name for the solemnity of the holy martyr Euphemia. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. We rejoice in this celebration, in which the blood of blessed Euphemia the martyr blossomed forth, illustrious through the fervor of the Holy Spirit and more precious than the frailty of her sex; and, striking down the rage of devilish persecution by feminine strength, virginity and passion achieved a triumph of doubled glory. Through, etc.

### II. Another

Receive, Lord, we ask, the sacrifices of the rejoicing Church, which, ready and willing, she has vowed to your majesty for the feast-day passion of Saint Euphemia the martyr. Through, etc.

[Col. 0103B] Truly it is worthy. As we recall the feast day of Saint Euphemia the martyr, we contemplate the wondrous reversal of events: the devil, who through the weakness of a woman had driven the man into ruin, was now, when the victory was restored by the man in Christ, crushed and cast down in turn through feminine weakness. [Note: [Col. 0103D] Here *mutata* or something similar seems to be missing.] Through, etc.

### III. Another

We offer you, Lord, the sacrifice of our service, which we owe for the honor of your name on the feast of Saint Euphemia the martyr. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. As we recall the joy of today’s feast, which the venerable confession of Saint Euphemia the martyr has made illustrious for us, [Col. 0103A] Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0103D] It is read in Muratori’s Gregorian codices in the Mass of the feast of Saint Euphemia; in Menardus and in the Roman Missal, on November 29, at the feast of Saint Saturninus.]

May reception of your sacrament sanctify us, Lord, we ask; and may the intercession of Saint Euphemia the martyr [Col. 0103C] make us acceptable to you. Through, etc.

May the humility of the Christian people rejoice, Lord, because in the commemoration of the holy martyrs it venerates your wonders and, aided by their prayers, may it please you. Through, etc.

## XXVI. The Day before the Kalends of October. The Feast of the Basilica of the Angel on the Salarian Way

[Note: [Col. 0103D] In both the Gelasian and Gregorian Sacramentaries this feast is recorded on the third day before the Kalends of October. The Gregorian codices give it the title “Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Angel” or “of Saint Michael.” In the most ancient Martyrology, as it is called, the Hieronymian, September 29 reads: “At Rome, six miles away, the dedication of the Basilica of Saint Michael,” which we recognize from our Sacramentary as having been established on the Salarian Way. Those who attribute this feast to Gelasius—not on account of the dedication of the basilica mentioned here, but on account of the apparition of Saint Michael on Mount Gargano—are later writers; their testimony should not be allowed to detract from the authority of our Sacramentary. [Col. 0104D]]

### I

Almighty and everlasting God, before whom the pious merits of every rational creature are always acceptable, yet before whom it is certain that those are more outstanding which surpass the rest in spiritual dignity: grant, we ask, that our celebration, offered in veneration of him who, preserving through your grace his natural beauty, is always near in devoted watchfulness to the mysteries of your majesty, may be pleasing to you. [Col. 0103D] Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0104D] It is read in the Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal on this day.]

We offer you sacrifices of praise, Lord, humbly asking that, through the intercession of the angel on our behalf, you may both graciously accept them and grant that they may come to our salvation. [Col. 0104A] Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. We proclaim you with overflowing joys on this day of today’s feast, on which sacred places have been established for divine mysteries in honor of blessed Michael the archangel and consecrated to your name. For although the dwelling of that sublime and glorious substance is always in heaven, nevertheless the devotion of your faithful presumes, out of reverence for your power, through these acts of pious devotion, to retain on earth a kind of pledge of the ministers who stand continually in your presence and serve you. And therefore, with the angels, etc.

### II. Another

[Note: [Col. 0104D] It is found in Book II, no. 59, of the Gelasian Sacramentary.]

Graciously accept, we ask, Lord, the gift of your people, which may be pleasing not through our merits, [Col. 0104B] but through the supplication of your holy archangel Michael. Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. To praise you as wonderful in all your creation, in which the angelic nature especially excels: although it is withdrawn from the bodily sight of the human race (another reading: denied to sight), it is nevertheless perceived by the gaze of faith. It is fitting that through honoring them we should behold your majesty, [Note: [Col. 0104D] Codex: *suscipere* (“to receive”).] through whom you perform many works of protection for our salvation, and that we should proclaim your magnificence especially because they confess you as Lord of the exalted and heavenly powers. Through, etc.

### III. Another

May our offering always be acceptable to you, Lord; through your angels and saints who pray, may it bring us forgiveness and obtain eternal remedies for us. [Col. 0104C] Through, etc.

Truly it is worthy. And even more so, not to be silent about your praises in the archangels and angels, because praise returns to your excellence and glory when the angelic creature, which, subject to your service from its creation, has proved acceptable, is honored; and when that creature is worthy of veneration, you show how immense you are and how far you surpass all things. Through, etc.

We have received the votive mysteries, Lord; we ask your mercy that through the prayers of those whose feast is celebrated with devotion they may become salutary for us. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0104D] The first part of this prayer, with several words inserted, has been transferred into the prayer “Defend,” among the common prayers of the Roman Missal for a congregation and family.]

Defend your family, Lord, and protect from the fear of enemies those who have prostrated themselves before you with their whole heart. May they not find your good gifts difficult, [Note: [Col. 0104D] Muratori, following Blanchinius’s conjecture, corrected this to *inveniat* (“may it find”) instead of *qua* (“for which”). But Blanchinius himself, in the corrections prefixed to the Sacramentary, advised retaining *inveniant* (“may they find”) instead of *in quibus* (“in which”), as the codex has it, since *familia* is a collective noun and can take the plural.] for both your saints and the angelic powers plead with you for them. Through, etc.

[Col. 0104D] ### IV. Another

God, who arrange both heavenly and earthly things for the aid of the human race, graciously refresh us, we ask, who labor in the lower part of the world, with the protection of the ministers above. [Col. 0105A] Through, etc.

In honor of blessed Michael the archangel, we frequent places dedicated to your name with mystical service. Grant, we ask, that we may rejoice in the intercession of those whose sublime merits we recount. Through, etc.

It is truly right. For you not only most graciously console us through the confessions of your saints, but also advance us into the companionship of the heavenly powers; you raise us up not only through the intercession of the martyrs, but also through the patronage of the angels themselves. Through, etc.

**101 V. Another [prayer].**—Lord, we bring forward the holy things of the saints. Since they are pleasing to you in the commemoration of all the righteous, we are confident that they are much more welcome in your sight when the angelic nature is venerated. [Col. 0105B] Through, etc.

It is truly right. For just as through your Apostle you graciously instruct us that our manner of life is already in heaven, so in your goodness you establish it, that we may be lifted there in mind, where those whom we venerate stand in attendance, and may strive toward the heights which, with devoted affection, we contemplate on the feast of the blessed archangel Michael. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0105D] In all the Gelasian and Gregorian Sacramentaries, and in the Roman Missal, this same prayer is read on this feast.] Strengthened by the intervention of the blessed archangel Michael, we beseech you, Lord, as suppliants, that we may reach in mind those whom we honor. Through, etc.

We beseech you, Lord, continually to guard your people in mercy, so that, always secure and aided by the necessary supports of spirits pleasing to you, they may always rejoice in pious veneration. Through, etc.

**XXVII. Admonition concerning the fast of the seventh month; and prayers and petitions.**

[Col. 0105C]

[Note: [Col. 0105D] This is found in the Roman Order in the proclamation of the fast of the tenth month.] Beloved, we must celebrate the annual feast of the fasts which the solemn recurrence of the seventh month announces. Therefore, on the Wednesday and Friday that follow, let us carry it out in the customary assemblies; on Saturday let us conduct the sacred vigils, so that, by suitable observance, supplicating the Lord with purified minds, and with the blessed apostle Peter interceding, we may deserve to be freed both from present dangers and likewise from those to come. Through, etc.

**I.**—[Note: [Col. 0105D] With these preceding words, with slight insertions, the fifth Lenten preface begins in the Vatican Gregorian manuscript according to Muratori. The Masses of this fast of the tenth month are also appended in the Gelasian codex to the Masses of Saint Michael.] O God, who do not allow sinners to perish until they turn and live, we beseech you to suspend the punishment due for our sins, and graciously grant that concealment may not heap up vengeance, but rather that amendment may contribute to pardon. Through, etc.

O God, defender and ruler of your people, graciously grant that, abstaining from every offense, we may be nourished with the necessities of life and delivered from hostile enemies. Through, etc.

[Col. 0106A] **Over the offerings.**—Almighty God, grant us to offer the sacrifice dedicated to your name with purified conduct. Through, etc.

It is truly right. For you have indeed beneficially imposed fasts upon us, [Note: [Col. 0105D] It seems that *indixisti* should be read.] by which, once the law of the flesh has been subdued, a purer spirit might emerge. Yet, when even in our very observances we are not free from harmful and illicit things, you testify through the prophetic word that this is not the fast you have chosen. For bodily chastisement cannot benefit us if our spirit is entangled in wicked thoughts; indeed, it is plainly worse if, while our earthly condition has been softened, the mind does not cease from iniquities. Therefore, Lord, graciously bestow upon us that, while suitable frugality is practiced outwardly, we may inwardly restrain ourselves from evil intentions, so that we may be able to exercise perfect self-control. Through, etc.

**After Communion.**—Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that we may always be occupied with your solemnities and may conform to their mysteries alike in mind and body. Through, etc.

**Over the people.**—[Note: [Col. 0105D] It is almost identical in the Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal on the Wednesday after Passion Sunday. In Gelasius it is found on Saturday.] O God who dwell within us, enlighten the hearts of your children sanctified by the fast, and graciously grant a merciful hearing to those who pray, to whom you grant the affection of devotion. Through, etc.

**II. Another [prayer].**—Hear our prayers, Lord, so that in every nation what was promised in the Gospel of your Word may be fulfilled, and that the fullness of adoption may obtain what the testimony of truth foretold. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0106D] It exists in Menardus for the fourth week before Christmas.] Attend, we beseech you, Lord, to this singular sacrifice, so that through participation in this mystery we may receive what we believe is to be hoped for, once it has been awaited. Through, etc.

It is truly right. For everything by which we live is yours. Although our nature has been corrupted by the wound of sin, it is nevertheless your work that those born for earthly things are reborn for heavenly ones.

Visit your family, we beseech you, Lord, and guard with watchful mercy the hearts dedicated to the sacred mysteries, so that the remedies of eternal salvation which, through your mercy, they receive, they may preserve under your protection. Through, etc.

**III. Another [prayer].**—Almighty and eternal God, in whose authority the rights of all kingdoms consist, protect everywhere the rulers of the Roman name, so that their desired prosperity may become the peace of your peoples. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0106D] In the margin of the codex: Before food.] Be present, Lord, with your faithful, and preserve from earthly dangers those whom you instruct with heavenly sacraments and to whom you grant bodily sustenance. [Note: [Col. 0106D] Blanchinius noted that the words “and to whom you grant bodily sustenance” are not a variant reading, as he had marked in his first studies and as Muratori suggested from the same source; for this prayer was to be said after the station had been completed, on the fast day, before food.] Through, etc.

Hear the prayers of your suppliants, Lord, and guard with perpetual protection those who serve you with devoted hearts, so that, hindered by no disturbances, we may always offer free service in the performance of our duties toward you. Through, etc.

It is truly right. You graciously deign to instruct rational creation, lest, devoted to temporal goods, it fail to strive toward eternal rewards, arranging things in such a way that it neither falls short through chastisement nor grows insolent through prosperity; but rather that its glorious devotion may become such [Note: [Col. 0107D] Blanchinius and Muratorius preferred *quod*] that it cannot be overcome when crushed by any adversities. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0107D] Two prayers have been made from this one. Almost the whole first part has been transferred into the prayer found in the Roman Missal among the common prayers for the living and the dead, and recited on Sundays and ferial days of Lent. The second part, beginning with the words “May this communion,” is found in the Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal on Monday of the Second Sunday of Lent, and elsewhere very often.] Almighty and eternal God, we humbly implore your mercy, that this sacrament of yours may not become for us guilt leading to punishment, but may become a saving intercession leading to pardon; may it be the removal of sins, the strength of the weak, and a firm bulwark against the dangers of the world. May this communion cleanse us from guilt and grant us to be participants in heavenly joy. Through, etc.

[Col. 0107B] **IV. Another [prayer].**—Grant us, we beseech you, Lord, rational action, so that, venerating you alone with a sincere mind, we may ask with greater confidence for what is yours and obtain it more easily. Through, etc.

Turn all our hearts toward you, Lord, we beseech you, so that, abstaining from the things by which you are offended, we may experience not your anger but your mercy. Through, etc.

Enlighten your gifts, O God their institutor, and through these offerings, by which you have wished to be appeased, mercifully sanctify those who offer them. Through, etc.

It is truly right. By whose power all things were created and by whose providence all things are governed. Therefore you rightly judged that we should be held by this law: that, if we do not fear you, under whom all things exist, we should fear all things; and conversely, that we should fear absolutely nothing if we faithfully revere you alone as the creator of all. Through, etc.

Grant us, almighty God, from whom every good comes, that, possessing you, we may lack no assistance. Through, etc.

Grant your people, our God, a will pleasing to you, because you will then bestow every prosperity upon them when you have made them suited to your ordinances. Through, etc.

**V. Another [prayer].**—[Note: [Col. 0107D] It is in the Gregorian codices and in the Roman Missal on the Wednesday after the Third Sunday of Advent.] Hasten, we beseech you, Lord; do not delay, and extend to us the protection of your mercy, so that those who trust in your compassion may be raised up by timely consolations. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0107D] It is read in the same manuscripts and in the Missal on the Third Sunday of Advent.] May the sacrifice of our devotion continually be offered to you, Lord, a sacrifice which both fulfills the ordinances of the sacred mystery and powerfully effects your salvation for us. [Col. 0107D] Through, etc.

It is truly right. And to proclaim your works with unceasing praises, because they are always just and good. They powerfully bring it about that rational wills either advance toward salvation amid these things or in no way complain against heavenly strength. Through, etc.

May the sacred food and saving drink be ours, Lord, we beseech you, food and drink which may strengthen temporal life and grant eternal life. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0108D] In the same codices and Missal it is found on the Thursday after the Second Sunday of Lent.] Be present, Lord, with your servants and grant your help to those who ask for it, so that, while they glory in you as author and governor, you may restore created things and preserve what has been restored. Through, etc.

**VI. Another [prayer].**—Almighty and eternal God, mercifully pour into our hearts that, restraining ourselves from earthly concerns, we may meditate more earnestly on heavenly things. Through, etc.

Repel, Lord, the many assaults which the world inflicts, so that we may be able to receive these heavenly gifts with tranquil thoughts. [Col. 0108B] Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0108D] Marginal notation in the codex: During the fast.] It is truly right. You command us to fast not only from bodily foods but also from the harmful pleasures of the soul itself. For if we reject bodily delicacies for this reason, lest we dull our spirit with blunted senses, how much more ought we to abstain from the excesses of the mind itself, so that, freed from disordered affections, it may be able to reach the splendor of heavenly light! Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0108D] It is in Gelasius, book II, no. 60, in Muratori’s Gregorian codices, and in the Roman Missal on the Wednesday after the Third Sunday of Advent.] Sated by your salvation, Lord, we humbly beseech you that we may be renewed in effect by what delights us in taste. Through, etc.

Grant salvation of mind and body to your people, Lord, and fill the hearts of your faithful with perpetual consolations, so that, refreshed inwardly and outwardly, they may both please you by their pious devotion and always obtain your benefits. Through, etc.

Grant, we beseech you, Lord our God, that we may be made fruitful in inward gifts, lest we deserve to lack outward supports. Through, etc.

**VII. Another [prayer].**—[Note: [Col. 0108D] Marginal note: During the fast. The Gregorian codices and the Roman Missal present this prayer during the fast of the seventh month, on Saturday.] Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that by fasting we may be filled with strength and, by abstaining, become stronger than all our enemies. Through, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0108D] It is in the same codices and Missal on the Friday of the fast of the seventh month. The Roman Missal repeats it on the Wednesday after the Third Sunday of Advent.] May the gifts of our fast be acceptable to you, Lord, we beseech you; may they both make us worthy of your grace by purifying us and lead us to eternal promises. Through, etc.

It is truly right. Your ineffable wisdom remains so unchangeably that in it kindness is not without the permanence of justice, nor justice without eternal goodness.
